title: Birthday of the Executioner
desc:
This morning witnessed a new batch of deaths of the regime's enslaved souls. At a time when the entire Orthodox Russian people celebrate Christmas, it is overshadowed by the figure of an executioner who will "celebrate" his birthday, the only one in broken Russia. This is the current dictator-executioner of Vorkuta - Vasily Blokhin. Usually on this day, the people of Vorkuta once again try not to go out into the streets, as numerous units of the Vorkuta NKVD look for "enemies of the state (regime)" everywhere, even in the sewers, and ruthlessly execute murders. Even those who work closely with the punitive squads, betraying their neighbors for their own reputation and safety, do not feel safe on this day.

More than 10 years have passed since Blokhin has ruled uncompromisingly at the top of this hell called Vorkuta. The system built by the NKVD faction continues to terrorize and destroy all manifestations of dissent or opposition to the Soviet government. Sirens whistle at 5 a.m. in concentration and gulag camps, signaling an 18-hour shift, even though on any other day it would have sounded at 6 a.m. and the working hours would have lasted 15 hours. Without a doubt, every year on January 7 there would be much more deaths than the usual daily ones, and yesterday's friends could be unsure of their survival on this day.

Although Blokhin could not physically visit all the spaces and complexes of the Vorkutlag in one day, given his advanced age, he began practicing the practice of "blood calls" a few years ago.On this day, according to the protocol, as soon as the chief woke up, the officers and supervisors of the "death camps" called him hourly, pragmatically congratulating their chief boss and asking if Vasily would "celebrate" his holiday in their gulag. Usually he was happy to agree, but today he was in no mood for anything.

His back hurt from the very morning, he had a headache, and today icy temperature was more than -20°C degrees in the capital Vorkuta. His age, 67 years old, made itself felt, even when he sought to drown his thirst for blood in the liquidation of "needs in the camps". No, he decided for the first time during his entire reign to finally open a hospital on the central street of Vorkuta, for himself and trusted persons. If he wanted to keep his possession and full control over the Vorkutlags, he had to take care of his health.

title: The Edge of The World
desc:
The usual frosty environment of the Arctic Urals meets a hundred new slaves, in particular Nenets, who were taken in a raid on the lands of thieves. From now on, these unfortunate souls will spend the rest of their lives in Vorkutlag, without the right to pardon. Because of what? They were simply unlucky to become neighbors of such a slave-owning country, whose politicians and leader have already forgotten what it means to rely on themselves.

Such are the realities of the current Russian anarchy - either survive or profit from the grief of others. The vast majority of new slaves will not survive 5 years in this nightmare. The youngest Danylo was only 18 years old, the oldest grandmother was 52 years old, but they were equal in terms of hard labor in the Ural mines and the icy north. Is this the equality promised by the Bolsheviks, or rather, its extremely distorted and contested version? All the prisoners understood that all these ideological beliefs or narratives did not matter here in the murderous systems of the Vorkutlags...

title: Arrival of Soviet Generals
desc:
These days postman Grigoriy tried to get to Vorkuta as soon as possible, because most of the shortest roads were covered with snow after the long snowfalls in January. Fortunately, the last route, although twice as long, was relatively unaffected by the weather. After driving non-stop for more than 32 hours in a row, he, very exhausted, arrived at the building of the most terrible person in the Tundra - the secretary of the Vokrutskyi NKVD.

Grigoriy is a local resident of the city of Vorkuta, he was never an opponent of the Soviet government, either because of empty dreams or because of despair that it would be worse under other regimes. However, living under the power of the NKVD, he was afraid to even think in an oppositional way, not to mention not fulfilling the instructions of some party figure. For his numerous career merits, he was promoted to one of several messengers of Blokhin.

In May 1961, he received his first important assignment - to arrange, through the mediation of Arseniy Golovko, the arrival of two generals from the WRRF. Already a month later, difficult negotiations continued, since the head of Vorkutlag had an ambiguous reputation. When Grigory was sure of the failure of the negotiations, Arseny somehow persuaded these generals to join the service. All four agreed that they would not reveal this information so as not to put the commander of the Northern Fleet at risk.

As a result, the secretary's messenger returned to Vorkuta in August that the generals agreed if they were given autonomy in managing the military units provided by him. A difficult decision was made at the end of 1961 - approving the demand. Grigoriy, again leaving for Arkhangelsk, informed the generals about Blokhin's approval of their demands, and personally laid out a route for them to safely reach Vorkuta with him.

When Grigory was sure of the failure of the negotiations, Arseny somehow persuaded these generals to join the service. All four agreed that they would not reveal this information so as not to put the commander of the Northern Fleet at risk.

As a result, the secretary's messenger returned to Vorkuta in August that the generals agreed if they were given autonomy in managing the military units provided by him. A difficult decision was made at the end of 1961 - approving the demand. Grigoriy, again leaving for Arkhangelsk, informed the generals about Blokhin's approval of their demands, and personally laid out a route for them to safely reach Vorkuta with him.

title: Maltsev's Plans for the Commission
desc:
Having assumed a new important position as new minister, based on the existing problem with the neglected state of logistics in the country, Comrade Mikhail reported to the secretary on his plan for the urgent restoration of this area. After analyzing the difficulties and high losses in the war against bandits, the new minister pointed out the lack of ways to secure and actually hold on to new territories. In conjunction with a broad partisan movement, the western-northern and southern parts of the Ural Mountains under our control should be connected in the short term.

The first phase of this plan involves preparing resources and creating a special commission to oversee regular road construction work. To this end, a clear financing mechanism must be established to prevent the corruption that exists under Yudin's schemes. These commissions will also audit expenditures to prevent theft and other abuses at the local level. All these steps will contribute to the fastest possible start of the work itself.

title: A New Beginning for Something Greater
desc:
With the end of military operations and the flames of brutal war and destruction in the north of Western Siberia extinguished, it seems that the bandits and criminal authorities, who represented complete lawlessness and anarchy, have been completely neutralized. The proud and ruthless NKVD soldiers completely destroyed the last organized armed cells of the criminal regime in the south, protecting the capital of Vorkuta and the Gulag system from destruction and liquidation. What began as a challenge to Blokhin's rule and our Gulags has now been subdued and subjugated. Dozens of nationalities, languages, and cultures, as expected, were unable to organize themselves to wage constant battles, skirmishes, or even hold the line of defense.

They are like sheep led by predators, a gangster mafia of criminals who cared not so much about our homeland as about their own wealth and skins. Indeed, these multinational reservists, hearing the first loud explosions of our post-war artillery and the sounds of our trucks loaded with disciplined infantrymen, immediately fled, disobeying orders. This anarchic structure collapsed, unable even to keep its most densely populated regions from being swiftly captured. Such unexpected military success and victory, which came with the onset of winter cold, pleased the old secretary. Was his state structure capable not only of surviving and defending itself, but also of defeating all enemies? Did the party bureaucracy now truly recognize his strength and indisputable authority? Was he capable of uniting the entire region of Western Siberia after this easy victory?

These were rhetorical questions he asked himself, questions that had already been answered during the Pechora War. Blokhin developed a plan to revive the new Union under his political and ideological structure, under his dictatorship. Yes, the main legitimate government of the Soviet Union after the collapse was the regime of Genrikh Yagoda and his NKVD in the Far East, but it would never have the strength not only to reach the Urals, but also to advance westward. Now north of the Ural Mountains from the west, and now east of it, the secretary realized his ability to surpass Yagoda from the East in all future endeavors and ultimately build his own Soviet Union.

He should not limit himself to Vorkuta or Western Siberia; now the stakes, like his ambitions, will extend to the entire Motherland and its human potential, which will allow Russia to finally take its rightful place in the club of world superpowers. The first step is the proclamation of the North Ural Soviet Government, and the second step will undoubtedly be...

title: The Admiral's Request Call
desc:
As we finance infrastructure projects across the country, other political groups have become more active in pursuing their own goals. They all operate secretly, making backroom deals and using these investment programs to their own advantage. Only one person decided to stand out from this gray mass of corrupt deals, none other than the country's chief admiral. The phone rang in the secretary's office, and when he picked it up, he was surprised to hear his only admiral, with whom he had last spoken on the phone on his birthday. - "Comrade Arseniy, what is the reason for your call? Is there another ship in need of repair?"

- "Comrade Secretary, good day. My call is not related to the fleet; everything is fine with it. I am calling about Maltsev's infrastructure plans. As you know, I have repeatedly proposed in recent years to allocate part of the state budget for the construction of a railway to the location of the Northern Fleet, the port of Usinsk. Since we're at war with the southern bandits, I strongly recommend using these funds to build this connection. It takes my crew a whole week to get to Vorkuta, not to mention the slow delivery of food and essential items. That is why my crew and I were so dependent on support from the WRRF, but that has to change, doesn't it?" - Golovko suggested.

After listening carefully and calculating the cost of this work, Blokhin wanted to refuse immediately, but the admiral's last words sounded like a threat to lose his valuable asset at sea. He didn't remember how many times he had refused the sailors' requests, five or ten times, but he was aware of their boiling anger against his own regime in the fleet. The moment of silence was broken first by a cough, and then by Vasily's response...

title: Easing of Forced Labor for the Captive Population
desc:
Our new administration in the newly acquired territories, which for several years were under the control of bandits, thieves, and criminal gangs, is facing numerous problems. Although the rebellious peoples and inhabitants of these lands cannot organize armed resistance to our authority, they are sabotaging our newly acquired industry in every way possible. The biggest problems come from Nyagan and Yugorsk, where, despite the presence of our patrols in these large cities, we cannot guarantee 100% safety for workers.

It's in our interest to declare local (not nationwide) martial law in the newly annexed territories and to introduce a curfew. Our Presidium of the Vorkutlag Council has proposed isolating the southeastern regions by moving some of the factories and personnel, including workers, to the safe north, closer to the Urals. In the short term, this will hurt our economic growth, but it will leave the remaining bandits in complete isolation, which will ultimately stop their active subversive activities.

On the other hand, there is a more aggressive and risky plan—to allow these bandits and saboteurs to seize factories in the region, but leave our explosive devices there. As a result, we will destroy most of their groups with a single push of a button, causing a series of explosions at their newly captured bases and coordination centers. This will also harm and frighten the civilian population, who will begin to take the new authorities seriously and obey them!

title: Unpleasant Realities
desc:
Work on laying the railway was proceeding almost according to plan, with only a month's delay, but roads had already been laid throughout Vorkuta. However, more state funds were being spent than expected. Suspicious that something was amiss, Maltsev instructed his loyal assistant Sergei Danilenko to investigate the audits and reports on expenditures and the redirection of funds. Twenty-four days later, Danilenko compiled a report on his investigation and arrived at the minister's office looking sad and rather perplexed.

- "Oh, Hello comrade Sergei, have you already completed my assignment to check the audits? Why are you silent? Is something not as we expected?" - minister did not understand his assistant's mood.
- "On the contrary, Mikhail Mitrofanovich, our suspicions about the commission have been confirmed. They have found loopholes, indirect ways to enrich themselves. Under this scheme, they frame other people when conducting audits, shifting responsibility to third parties who are completely innocent. As a result of their own secret machinations, taking advantage of innocent souls and effectively condemning them to execution, they steal state funds from road construction financing with the useful intention of enriching themselves..." - Sergei summed up his successful investigation.

Maltsev almost fell to the ground when he heard this, because if this information came to light and became known to Vorkutlag's Chief, the same thing could happen to him as to his predecessor. Visibly sweating and glancing around to make sure the door to his office was tightly closed, he whispered to his assistant:

- "We're in deep trouble, because it was my initiative to set up the commission. Keep quiet about this investigation, don't say a word to anyone. I myself will slowly, carefully, and gradually fire and get rid of all these corrupt bastards. Your job is to watch the members of this commission 24/7 and report to me on their every move until they are all gone."

title: Breaking Human Will
desc:
It was late at night, almost 4 a.m., and most of the country's population was already asleep, except for a group of special forces called "Fortress" from Blokhin's NKVD. The group of 28 soldiers received orders that night to carry out an "unexpected finishing blow" against the mafia gangs in Yugorsk. The targets were practically objects throughout the city, some of which were not even occupied by these groups. They divided into seven groups of four soldiers each and set off to their posts to carry out the task.

Sergeant Dmitry Ivanov's group was assigned the most important point - the railway junction connecting Yugorsk with the rest of the country. This connection was the only link to the capital, Vorkuta, and its destruction would mean that hundreds of thousands of the city's residents would be isolated, without communications or electricity. Twenty minutes later, the detachment was already at the task site, and Dmitry took the floor:

- "Comrades, we have a unique opportunity to cut off the forces of the vile mafia gangs from reinforcements from the surrounding villages. This will finally put an end to their long reign of terror and resistance to the law and our liberating power. So, who wants to start blowing up the railway station and the nearest bases where the bandits are located?" In response, Vladimir and Vlad wanted to take advantage of this unique opportunity. But the fourth, ordinary member of the group, Sergei Antonov, had doubts and remained silent. Dmitry looked at the ordinary member, calling on him to press the lever that would cause a series of explosions.

- “Comrade Dmitry Ivanov, but won't this explosion isolate the peaceful citizens of the city from our civilization? Such explosions will cause civilian casualties and cut them off from our communications and power grid and...", Sergei said, but was interrupted by the sergeant.

- "Comrade Sergei, we are all following orders from above. The survival of our state is at stake, and if we have to sacrifice a few thousand civilians for that, we will do it! We are not some weak Red Army that suffered defeats in the war not only against the Germans, but even against Russian bandits. We must change, or we will simply suffer defeat after defeat! Now, be a conscious NKVD soldier and carry out this order without further ado..." cut in the sergeant.

Such are the realities of Russia today. In fact, Sergei knew that his opinion would not be heard either now or in the future. All orders in the NKVD must be obeyed, so, closing his eyes, Sergei pushed the lever all the way down.

title: Domestic Political Issues
desc:
A meeting is held with the NKVD to deal with the instability in the region. The main reason why this meeting of the ruling party was convened is the disturbing news from the south. Based on the results of our reconnaissance in the heart of our natural enemy, the bandits in Yugorsk, we received information about their preparations for hostilities against us. Blokhin guessed this, since the number of border skirmishes and provocations from [YGR.GetNameWithFlag] over the past two years has increased several times compared to previous years.

So prominent members of the left and central wing of the Vorkuta NKVD, Vsevolod Merkulov and Sergey Kruglov, decided to convene a party meeting at the beginning of 1962 to decide on a strategy to counter these southern bandits. Vasily personally hates them the most, calling for the fastest destruction of their homeland, first of all, to maintain his power and control in Vorkuta. Vsevolod and Sergey, more gradual in this opposition, call for and present worthy arguments against direct action against the leader of Yugra, Jaba Ioseliani.

"They should not even guess about our awareness of their plans and our preparation for a clash. By multiplying our presence on their border, we risk exposing ourselves!" - Merkulov said. "Instead of increasing only military production, I urge you to accept my economic plans. They will generally improve our production capacity and contribute to our industrial revolution in the long run! And we will not only have the terrible slaves and thugs of russian anarchy, but also more formidable forces - nationalists, monarchists and others."

Kruglov nodded at the presented arguments of his colleague, but they both understood that the final decision was Blokhin's. The best outcome they could hope for now was a compromise, as the thirst for blood had to be realized in one form or another in Western Siberia...

title: Dominant Position in the Party
desc:
In his usual past political routine, Blokhin had to get the support of the party council purely symbolically. Usually, at the beginning of his career as the head of Vorkutlag in the 50s, he had to consult with others to identify potential political opponents, oppositionists. In some places, there were cases of "enemies of the country" being found, and in the next few hours they were already lying dead in an unmarked grave. However, with the beginning of the 60s, there were no non-bolshevik elements left in the political system of Vorkuta, the country became completely totalitarian.

In such a system, you either obey and cooperate with the government, or you end up in prison on a quickly fabricated case. When it comes to the fabrication of compromising material against dissidents and "enemies of the state", NKVD employees have no equal. They can trivially create so much false information about a person in one night that he will be in danger of being shot the next morning. An active executive role in the Vorkuta NKVD is played behind the scenes by Sergey Kruglov, who, fearing for his own life, carries out any bloody whims of Blokhin.

However, other, more conscious elements in the party emphasize that this state of affairs threatens sooner or later to result in a nationwide russian anti-bolshevik uprising, which will overthrow this entire existing anti-human system. Therefore, until it is too late, Merkulov and Golovko call on Vasily Blokhin to find another way to manage the country, first of all, to preserve his sole and party power in the years to come, putting the role of the NKVD on the back burner. According to their plan, the old bureaucrats, who have proven their reliability and efficiency in service at times, should be returned to the foreground, before the collapse of the Union.

title: Old Union Bureaucrats
desc:
When considering the issues of old party figures of the VKP(b) Vasily Blokhin, mixed feelings are often enveloped. On the one hand, it is a pity that Russia is now in such decline, thrown into the dustbin of history. On the other hand, only thanks to the collapse of the Soviet Union, Blokhin is here now, undividedly ruling over the russian tundra.

The only question that worried him all the last years was whether it would be eternal? Vorkuta is surrounded by many enemies, and if today everything is peaceful and no one wants to get a frozen piece of russian tundra in the northern Urals, then what will happen tomorrow? The bandits of Yugra will be crushed, that's for sure, but will the terror methods of the NKVD be enough for this? Old Soviet bureaucrats who want to rebuild their ruined careers answer these long and open questions. In these new realities, they are not accepted by other Soviet governments, having found the only political refuge in Vorkuta.

The Secretary's policy has always been vague on this point. These losers, guilty of numerous uprisings and the final collapse of the Soviet Union, were neither persecuted nor allowed to rule here. title: Appointment of a New Minister of Economy
desc:
"Comrade Yevgeniy, sit down opposite me, we need to talk", - Vasily said bluntly to his economy minister, without even greeting him when the latter entered the square office of the most terrifying man, whose cruelty knew no bounds. Visibly sweating, the minister sat down on a broken chair, angry at himself for not having replaced the furniture in the Vorkuta government offices in the previous months. This meant that the conversation could not be pleasant or neutral.

"G-good health, our secretary..." - Yudin replied in a slightly trembling voice, "...I am very s-sorry for the unresolved issue regarding the furniture in our party's government building. Our l-limited resources, in accordance with your urgent o-order regarding the construction of a hospital, were directed toward this endeavor..."

"That doesn't matter, because given the lack of weapons for our army, combined with the difficult situation with electricity supply, I am dismissing you right now. All your property and assets will be confiscated for state needs," Secretary Blokhin stated bluntly. At that moment, Yevgeniy Yudin's whole world collapsed. The profits and benefits he had gained from his position since the West Siberian People's Republic lost control of Vorkuta became meaningless. However, right now, one emotion was raging - fear. He knew what happened in such cases; no one returned alive from the party building after being dismissed from the post of minister.

When he tried to get up to run away, the chair broke, knocking Yudin to the floor, where three of Blokhin's guards, who had been waiting for orders from outside, rushed to him. "Yevgeniy Yudin, for your numerous financial machinations, which I have learned about, as well as lies in reports on the electrification of the entire country, you are declared an enemy of the state, and the punishment for this is execution. The order will be carried out the day after tomorrow. It's a pity that I had to deal with you all these years," Vasily said in a cold, ruthless tone.

"Damn you, may this cursed country burn in hell, and may your entire structure be destroyed and forever forgotten in the pages of history, you scoundrel Blokhin! See you in hell, you animal!" were Yudin's last words as he was led out of the office and the door closed.

Sitting down at his desk and drinking some mineral water, Vasily called Vsevolod and told him that the candidate he had proposed for the post of Minister of Economy could take office as of today.

title: Blokhin System
desc:
It seems that all events led to this, as if fate itself had led to this outcome. The appointment of Blokhin as head of the Vorkuta branch of the Gulag, the party turning a blind eye to his atrocities, the collapse of the Soviet Union. Indeed, not only was he not hindered, but they also kept quiet or cooperated with him. In this northern Russian Arctic tundra, there is now only one set of rules - his.

The lifestyle of ordinary residents is worse than under any other communist regime in the ruins of the Union. In this country, you either work for the good of society in freedom, or you work in prison, or you work in the Gulag, and so on. Life is work, and work is the viability of Blokhin's regime. And if someone is dissatisfied with something, they may get a "pleasant" short conversation with NKVD agents.

Other journalists, according to the North Ural Soviet government, are not allowed to travel independently throughout the country. It is strictly forbidden to mention the life of the ordinary population, and upon arrival and departure from the country, foreigners are searched for "prohibited literature and information" that could even hint at harming the regime. If suspected of being an "enemy of the regime", such individuals are either tortured for a very long time to extract "imaginary" information or shot. Those who survive after being branded as such envy the dead, because the dead do not want to eat...

title: Monolithic Prisons of the South
desc:
Non-Russian minorities settled in the vast expanses of southern Yugorsk, including Jews. Life in Vorakh Yugra was turbulent, with residents living according to the "code" of thieves law and untouched by the state or mafia gangs. Two childhood friends, David and Benjamin, grew up in these conditions. They were 18 and 19 years old, respectively, when the Pechora War began. Their Jewish families did not want to leave their property, so they remained in the village-type town of Malinovsky, right before the war.

What began as a defense quickly turned into the defeat of the bandit and mafia army, and units of the Northern Red Army reached the city without a fight. The policy of the new communist administration was simple:all able-bodied people, including young men who had already turned 18 by the time the Bolsheviks arrived, were forcibly taken to work in "labor camps", namely the Gulag. Local families were told that this was "temporary, for 1-2 years", and those who did not agree were threatened with repression. In the next two and a half weeks, David and Veniamin were transferred to the Pechora Gulag, where riots and prisoner uprisings broke out, leading to war.

The first month in this hell was the worst, due to the inadequate 21/7 work regime and infrequent meals (twice a day). However, the newly arrived "labor prisoners" were promised that if they stayed in this complex for 18 months in a row, working and without disciplinary violations, they would be released to their families. They were not told whether they would be released permanently or temporarily. People of all nationalities worked here, from Caucasians to Kazakhs and Mongols.

However, after a month, David was taken to another Gulag - Vorkuta - for receiving three disciplinary violations. Veniamin heard nothing more and could not find out about the fate of his childhood friend, but in this godless place he could hope in his god, Judas, who would not forget his followers and would save them from death. But there is definitely light at the end of the dark tunnel, from which there seems to be no way out; you just have to keep working.

title: Agreement with Aviators
desc:
After defeating our main rivals in Yugra, we gained a border with an important neighbour - the Free Aviators. This is one of those rare cases in the ruins of Russia where the warlords are predominantly women - female pilots. Compared to the bandits and mafia we fought for several months and who generally had substantial armed forces, the Surgut authorities of the Nenets minority have, at best, a few thousand soldiers. Their army is armed with outdated weapons, such as the PPSh-41, and has no light or heavy equipment, so their defeat is only a matter of time.

Another issue is that they have aircraft and the 588th Night Bomber Regiment is stationed in Surgut. If direct military offensive actions are taken, these pilots will either destroy their aircraft or flee eastward to Siberia. Not to mention the damage to aircraft during active combat. That is why the secretary decides to send his foreign minister, Boris Trofimov, to Surgut for negotiations. Their future fate in the newly restored Union will depend on their response!

title: Delegation from the Northern Ural Soviet Government
desc:
Foreign Minister Boris Trofimov from the Ural Northern Soviet Government has arrived and is proposing that we integrate into this newly formed successor state to the Soviet Union. We have had no previous ties with them, but their brilliant victory in the war against the formidable bandits of Yugra gives us pause for thought.

We do not have a large armed force, and those we do have are equipped with outdated weapons. We cannot win with just our air force and bombers, and it is unlikely that the Sverdlovsk District will come to our aid, as they have not yet completed their military preparations. In this situation, we are alone, so we must either seek compromises or evacuate our forces and administration from Surgut, flying further east to Siberia or the Far East (if we have enough fuel).

title: Bocharova Agrees to Integration
desc:
About five days after his departure, Trofimov returned to Vorkuta with good news. The secretary urgently interrupted his meeting on energy issues in the country and invited the returning delegation to his office. "Bocharova has agreed to the peaceful integration of her domain in exchange for the enshrinement of women's rights in our legislation and the future Constitution of the Union, putting them on an equal footing with men. In return, they will join our new air force and transfer all their aircraft to us", Boris announced joyfully.

This was a perfectly acceptable outcome for Blokhin, if one disregards the equalisation of rights in the Communist Party. In the current uncertain situation in Western Siberia and the trials that lie ahead, the end justifies the means. He will make an exception, only in this situation of Russia's split, accepting representatives of the ‘Free Aviators’ into the party apparatus, even if they are all women. But these people will not get any further, and if the majority of them demand political change, he will fabricate cases against them, using his NKVD structure.

desc:
About a week after the negotiations, Minister Trofimov returned to Vorkuta with his delegation. In order to receive them, the secretary had to interrupt his meeting with representatives of national minorities from the new territories and invite Boris to give a report. With a blank stare, he began his report: "Comrade Chief Secretary, in their final response to our peaceful proposal, Yevdokia categorically refused, comparing us to the tyrants in Omsk and stating that our actions would ultimately destroy Russia from within and incur countless enemies after unification, and that they would rather flee to the east than serve us...".

After finishing this report, after a half-minute pause, Blokhin asked to inform the Minister of Defence and the entire military command, because they ‘know what to do in such a situation,’ and asked the entire team that had returned and Trofimov to leave the office. Upon leaving the Presidium building, Boris heard shouting and rumbling from the secretary's office on the street, which meant only one thing.

title: Unexpected Uprising in the Gulags!
desc:
With the start of large-scale combat clashes with units of the Thief Territory of Yugra, as well as the lightning-fast advance of our brigades in the Salekhard direction, things did not go according to plan. Due to the lack of additional reservists, the military force we assembled consisted mainly of guards from a number of Gulags, most of whom were taken from the west and the border with the WRRF, where we had been in local security before the war. If anything could have gone wrong, our partners in Arkhangelsk would have covered us, but the reality turned out to be different.

Several dozen key figures among the prisoners, taking advantage of their numerical superiority over our reduced guard force, successfully staged an uprising and captured several neighboring detention centers. We officially requested armed support from the WRRF, as well as the involvement of their weakened but still existing Red Army to deal with these “bandit scoundrels”, but the response was negative. Citing stretched garrisons and internal strife between two marshals, they effectively abandoned us to our fate! The worst part is that, apart from them, we have no one to defend us, and from now on we are alone against all our current and future enemies!

From the official declaration of the prisoners' elected leader, Stasys Ignatavičius, it became clear that they do not intend to lay down their arms and surrender, stating the opposite, that they are ready to lay down their lives for freedom!
"There was shooting and a takeover in the camp... 16 guards and 7 prisoners were killed... The prisoners were not satisfied with this, so I addressed the prisoners in barrack 21 and asked them to gather the elders and form a committee to restore order in the camp and prepare for defense... Two deputies and one chairman should be elected, of whom I will be your chairman sisters and brothers, and I will ask for help from friendly Yugra!" proclaimed Stasys.

Given the chaotic start of the Pechora War and the first day of its duration, we cannot be completely sure of our victory. However, our army is better armed than the enemy's and loyal to the secretary, not to money, like those mafiosi from Yugorsk... Either we will be victorious, or anarchy will reign supreme in Russia for a long time to come.

title: Vorkuta.event.26.t
desc:
Today, the secretary`s agenda included a plenary meeting of the Party, at which he wanted to raise a topic that was unexpected for everyone. Such meetings are traditionally held in the capital city of Vorkuta, where traffic and pedestrians are restricted around the Presidium building, and virtually everything around it comes to a standstill. There have never been any loud noises, repair crews, or anything else that could distract the attention of influential members of the regime, and this meeting will be no exception. One of the features that had not been characteristic of the Presidium until now was the presence of a female member, for whom this was a first: Zeya Voskresenskaya. As a member of the Surgut Night Witches squadron, without instructions from the local authorities, upon receiving information about the arrival of a delegation from the North Ural Soviet government, she took her plane at her own discretion and flew across the border, landing at the Nyagan airport. She voluntarily surrendered to our garrison and declared that she was switching sides and requesting amnesty. In less than three weeks, Zoya was in the Presidium building, with the personal approval of the secretary, which was remarkable because it was the first time a female aviator had become a party deputy in such a short period of time, giving her the opportunity to attend the meeting.

Of course, because of this, many people disliked her, looked at her askance, and considered her unexpected appearance a “gift of fate.” Nevertheless, the buzz in the hall ceased when the ministers entered the room, the first of whom was Trohimov, who had just returned from a diplomatic mission in Surgut. First of all, he officially introduced Zoya to other party leaders as a “brave aviator who voluntarily chose the side of the legitimate Soviet government,” thus demonstrating her commitment to the ideals of the communist revolution. It was hard not to notice the absence of Minister Maltsev at the meeting, who was too busy with infrastructure upgrades and the construction of a new railway outside Vorkutlag. Ten minutes later, Vasily Blokhin, the head of the regime and the government of the newly emerging Union, entered the hall to a standing ovation as he made his way to the podium. Coughing noticeably, but walking confidently and without faltering, he took his place at the large semicircular table, pulled up a comfortable chair specially made for him, sat down, waited a few seconds for the applause to die down, and began to read his prepared speech:

"My dear members of the Presidium, members of our newly proclaimed North Ural Soviet Government, today I have gathered you all not just to discuss such complex issues as food, finance and economics, migration... *cough*... integration, the army, or anything along those lines. First of all, I would like to highlight our main achievement over the past year - namely, the defeat of our natural enemy, who could have destroyed us if he had gathered more strength - the bandits of Yugra, which allowed us to proclaim ourselves the official heirs of the Soviet Union!" Numerous applause rang out in the hall, some even shed tears of joy, among them was Zoya.
"In view of this, we must not... *cough*... stop. I have already instructed my government to develop a strategy for our further actions to defeat other competitors to our power in the region. However, the most important issue, for which I have gathered you all here today, must be resolved. *Cough*... So, we are talking about restoring order within, that is, in our hearts, so that they do not waver and do not let our country down on the path to uniting all of Western Siberia!" The hall erupted in another round of collective applause, either in complete agreement with the secretary's position or out of fear that those who did not applaud would attract the attention of the law enforcement services.
"Comrades, this is a necessary step for our security and strength. I will instruct the NKVD officers under my command to conduct searches of your offices and, if necessary, your homes or apartments, to ensure your true loyalty and devotion to my... *cough*... cause. You have no reason to worry if you have nothing to hide. Everyone must work without hiding anything, as a single mechanism for restoring our long-lost Soviet heritage! Glory to the NKVD Party of the North Ural Soviet Government, forward to complete victory over the bourgeoisie and counter-revolutionary elements!“ ”Glory forever!" - resounded the long, enthusiastic applause of the standing party members, some of whom were visibly sweaty.

The secretary stood up and left the hall, followed by everyone else. Some were wildly happy about the unexpected checks against their opponents, such as Voskresenskaya and Garanin, who now had an extra chance to demonstrate their loyalty. Others, such as Merkulov and Trohimov, were somewhat concerned about the resumption of the old course of checks and surveillance of the movements of each party member, but everyone understood Blokhin's next steps. There would be no expansion to the south until all doubts about the absence of subversive elements within the party had completely disappeared. All members of the Presidium just had to get through this period and wait for the regime's attention to shift to other, external threats, which would inevitably come to the fore sooner or later.

title: Formal procedure, personal Constitution
desc:
One more meeting, one more agreement, and now the full Presidium is gathering for the adoption of the Constitution of the West Siberian Workers' Republic. Everyone is traditionally waiting for the appearance of the Secretary for this important event for the whole country, because before the unification of the whole of Western Siberia, there were no Constitutions. Since its content, although it legally enshrines such traditional unlimited powers for Blokhin, such as personal control over domestic and foreign policy, the jurisdiction of the Presidium's judicial power is officially defined here.

Throughout his reign, he did not show much interest in the courts, as they were a rare phenomenon, present only in the city of Vorkuta, the only one that tried only party figures who were against the regime. The ordinary population was tried by field military courts on the ground, which significantly reduced the burden on administrative costs, since the decisions were carried out on the ground without bureaucratic red tape, postponements of cases, and so on. This is the most interesting aspect of the adoption of the constitution, because now, ironically (given all the purges), the courts become under the control of the Presidium as a reward for the regime's service. Nevertheless, this does not mean that the dictator loses some degree of control over this direction, because the judges will be those who can be trusted.

Looking at such a compromise, even Merkulov's socialist party faction is ready to vote for the current project in its entirety.The only thing that worries some party members is the announcement of a "securocratic-workerist revolution" in the Soviet Labor Republic, as it is about a radical program of actions for the next few years. Despite this, Vasily Blokhin enters the hall to applause and sits down at the podium. Then, declaring this day "the day of restoration of the long-lost dogmas of Russian labor", and looking around everyone, permission was given to hold the vote.

Despite all the disadvantages and negative long-term consequences for the country, the party leaders were well aware of the alternative of rotting and cold death in the Gulag somewhere in the hinterland of the isolated tundra, so everyone, like one solid well-oiled mechanism, voted "for" the new tyrannical Constitution, which would secure Blokhin's status as a dictator for life. After 40 seconds, the winds changed direction, the dogs barked, a few apoliticians broke into a sweat, and the tyrant smiled wryly and began to clap his hands wildly, urging everyone to start doing the same, idolizing his figure in that moment for the flashes of the camera lenses. Soon, the next day, the entire capital received a fresh newspaper "Pravda" with a picture of the Presidium's unanimous vote for the new Constitution with the headline: "Secretary Blokhin started the Labor Revolution, to the horror of the bourgeoisie!".

title: Invisible Warriors
desc:
The only source of causing real damage to challenger rivals in the region, subversive sabotage became almost the main tool in Blokhin's hands. Over the past few months, special cells of agents have been formed in several Russian states at once, with particular attention paid to the largest of them. It is those that pose the primary danger to the existence and survival of our country - the Ural Military District and the Tyumen Soviet Administration. Accordingly, we have been preparing the ground for the start of acts of sabotage just when new wars will begin in the region, and it seems that time has come. In order not to risk our assets and trained agents in the field of covert missions, we use local civilians who are looking for "easy money" and are willing to cooperate with "people's avengers" (our undercover agents) against unpopular local authorities. The targets of our operations are not provincial towns or villages far from administrative centers, but on the contrary, the places closest to them. 2 main directions can be distinguished from them:

1) Instead of sabotage of administrative buildings, which will quickly attract the attention of local administrations and leaders, the main goal will be the partial or complete disabling, i.e. destruction, of thermal power plants. This approach will ensure energy instability in the enemy's power grid and chaos in communication with field commanders on the battlefield.Through our own mistakes, we have learned the criticality of the lack of a working power grid for the operation of the state apparatus and effective management of the country, and we can use this technique against our enemies.
The most favorable period for the operation: Winter or early spring, which will also cause unrest among civilians. In this case, part of the units of the enemy army will be redeployed from the battlefield deep into their own territory in order to prevent further escalation of the situation into an anti-government uprising.
Estimated costs: The costs significantly exceed the expected forecasts of 420 million rubles, because they include not only the planning and issuance of all the necessary funds to our agents for the implementation of such an operation, but also leaving a reserve in case it will not be possible to carry out the plan in some areas. Such contingencies will require the emergency evacuation of our agents from enemy territory to avoid detection.

2) For another, safer direction of sabotage, we choose the enemy's infrastructure, railway tracks and other logistical nodes of the enemy's communication. Such actions will have less effect on the battlefield, but will definitely undermine the financial reserve position in the short term for our enemies. This approach should ensure that local administrations and leaders spend priority budgets not on the military, but on the fastest possible repair of logistical connections in their territories, which will allow us to win the war of attrition without problems.
The most favorable period for the operation: Late spring or summer, just when the holiday seasons will begin, or when it will be necessary for military units to quickly use the railway to counterbalance the roads, which are in an impassable, damaged state.
Estimated costs: The costs should not exceed the expected, up to 370 million rubles for the planning, implementation and completion of the operation by our agents, who were well trained during the activity of exterminating partisan movements from the former Thief Territory of Yugra. It is also worth noting the lack of proper security teams along the entire section of communication routes, which means a much lower chance of exposing our agents, especially compared to the first direction of the aforementioned sabotage operation.

The conclusion of the report:
The Special Subversive Group "Heads of Punishment" recommends that no expense be spared in carrying out the above-mentioned operations, taking into account the agents' professional training, professional training in planning every aspect of the operations, and the motivation and desire to help the ruling regime and government in defeating traitors, apostates and bourgeois-imperialists in the region who only want to sell Russia to insidious foreigners. In the case of approval by the Presidium and the respected Secretary of one of the operations, the "Heads of Punishment" will immediately begin the implementation of the operation plan, aimed at weakening and eliminating the threat to our country of an enemy contender for complete control in the region.

End of report.

title: Priorities Given When Updating the Army Model
desc:
After a busy first half of the day, in which he had to write orders for several political reshuffles in the Ministry of Internal Affairs, the secretary leaned back in his chair. It was already lunch time, so he didn't hesitate for a long time, stood up, locked his office and sat back, taking out his lunch from the drawer. A little over 1 hour passed when he got his spaghetti with baked chicken. It wasn't as warm as it had been right after cooking, but he didn't care. He ate his lunch in 30 minutes, and decided to walk through the corridors of the Government. Today was Friday, but to his surprise the building was filled with civil servants. Having not even reached the stairs to go down to the lower floor, Merkulov flew up to him, asking for an immediate discussion of the future army reforms, taking into account the soon end of the working day.

Although Vasily was irritated by such abruptness, he was still aware of the importance and urgency of this issue. The war for the unification of the region was difficult, there were many casualties, and an atmosphere of mistrust still reigned in the army structure. Their distrust was not of generals or commanders, not at all, on the contrary, of each other, and everyone in the government understood this, including the leader of the Union. Both of them went into the office, spreading out their documents, and sitting down with an expectant expression on their faces, Blokhin gave the floor to the leader of the reformist parties.

"Comrade Secretary, as I wrote to you in the reports from the beginning of the week, we should seriously engage in reforms in the army to reduce the dissatisfaction of servicemen. Since we already have two working models in the army, I suggest that you make one of two decisions on this issue.", a short pause in connection with turning the pages of the notebook.

"Look, I fully support with both hands the use of the previous model of the Red Army, which was used in the Soviet Union. According to it, we equalize the rights and privileges that mainly only NKVD units have, our other armed units...which will allow us to achieve full loyalty and support from the military side and towards the ruling regime. I would like to point out that we are not talking about the return of everything old, which is why the old Union actually lost the Great Patriotic War, but the combination of only the positive experience of the NKVD gained during recent wars, with the political will to apply it all at the level of the entire army.", looking up from the notebook at the old man in front of him, and catching his unbearable gaze, the description of the reform model was finished.

"Comrade Vsevolod, and yet, yesterday I read your alternative summary about using the NKVD model as the main one. Accordingly, it attracted my attention first, and I liked it more in its core. And now, you want to convince me to accept this Bolshevik model, because of which we lost the war, mixing it with the discipline and loyalty of the NKVD for the illusory positive result of the "Elite Red Army"? You know, you really don't understand, thanks to whom we can enjoy the full view of the Urals, the machine-building plants of Chelyabinsk, or be in the "megapolis" of Sverdlovsk," the Secretary answered abruptly.

Vsevolod anticipated this answer, so in the next two and a half hours, he read over and over all his arguments in the notebook that he had been preparing since the beginning of the week.The bet is not on understanding, but on the fatigue of the tyrant, who will not be able to postpone this issue to another day, because he understands its urgency. Now everything depends on the incessant rhetoric and facts of the narrator regarding the prospects of the state of the army, after adopting the model of the updated Red Army. It was already dark, and finally, unable to listen to all this any longer, the secretary gave his final answer:

title: A Question of Expediency
desc:
Marshal Roman Ivanov sat at his desk, two lists sitting before him, columns and rows extending endlessly, filled with names in professional typeface, no doubt created by some little beady eyed freak in the Security Department.

He sighed, rubbing his eyes. The problem seemed so daunting, so large, and yet, at its core, when reduced to its simplest components, it was actually quite simple. The Free Aviators, a nominally socialist but practical apolitical body that did its best, over the course of twenty years, to protect the people of Russia from the German bombers who plagued their broken, battered country, had been swallowed by the military rather quickly. They had accepted their rule as a better alternative to the anarchy that harmed Russia. But the problem wasn't their competence, which no self respecting man or woman could deny. Rather, it was a question of politics.

Roman received word from up high that Secretary and his lackeys didn't like a lot of the aviators. Not enough to purge them, no, they were too popular for that, but just to prevent them from gaining any real power or influence in the nascent Air Force. And so created the conundrum: should he promote the names on the left list, a less competent, but more politically safe option of figures, or the right list, the Aviators, consequences be damned. Choices, choices.

After several hours, he decided...

desc: We have received a radio broadcast from Sverdlovsk in Western Siberia from a socialist regime known as the West Siberian Soviet Labor Republic. This state is led by the local head of the NKVD, Vasily Blokhin. While they boast the almost same policies and even government ministers as the old Soviet government, it also unsurprisingly appears that the NKVD plays a large role in Russian society, with the police state and surveillance being extensive. Blokhin claims this is a temporary measure to preserve socialism in the state, and that he will lessen the NKVD grip on society once the situation stabilises and all enemies of the state will be defeated; however, the question of whether to support an extensive police state with ties to the old Soviet government remains.

title: Intentions and Ambitions that are Just a Matter of Time
desc:
In our tumultuous times, the world is ruled by force or by its own economic superiority over others. Since our motherland, due to a large number of factors, including disintegration, lost and fell behind economically several decades ago, we have a tiny chance of becoming an economic hegemon. Even such insignificant and secondary countries as Brazil have overtaken us and firmly occupied a place in the top 10 most successful economies in the world. Under such conditions, we can rely only on our strength and cunning in the implementation of our power projections on neighboring countries.

Although the language, like our goals and focus, is directed only to the reunification of our homeland, we cannot be irresponsible in spending our resources around the world at the same time. Now, we will focus on specific targets that correspond to our strategic geopolitical interests. Thus, our Secretary is confident that we will achieve, in the short term, the goals of our national interest for the long-term survival of our Union. Also, all our ministers and party figures will do everything possible to preserve and strengthen our sphere of influence, on which our future existence depends!

title: Heartland of the WSSLR
desc:
Upon proclaiming the establishment of the West Siberian Soviet Labor Republic, we were faced with an extremely heavy administrative burden. And this is not a matter of a shortage of officials, governors, or police, but rather of the remoteness of our main capital. All politicians, including ministers, are concerned about the remoteness of our capital - the city of Vorkuta - from Western Siberia itself. After all, the city is located northwest of the Ural Mountains, which has now become our Achilles' heel. No one doubts anymore that if military hostilities break out with our western rival vying for control over West Russia - and the question is rather "when" this will happen - it will happen. And the Secretary himself realizes the futility of leaving the capital in the distant Arctic Russian north, a region unsuitable for normal life without the risk of frostbite.

However, this is where disagreements arise, as all sides are proposing several mutually exclusive options at once. Real power lies in the hands of a few, so we can identify three realistic proposals that have defined the so-called "capital triangle". Trofimov coined this term in reference to the location of the cities - potential leading candidates for capital status. The most discussed and widely supported among them are Sverdlovsk, Chelyabinsk, and Zlatoust, which form the so-called "capital triangle". Only one city will receive the sole and permanent status of capital, to which the Presidium along with the party, officials, all law enforcement agencies, and our main government institutions will be relocated.

The city of Sverdlovsk is the most popular choice - our Party's proposal, championed by the leader of the Socialist-Reformists, Vsevolod Merkulov. To our surprise, this option has been supported by both our Red Guard and the apolitical faction, sailors. Citing its advantageous geographical location and its position at the intersection of all major transportation routes in West Siberia, this choice is the ideal option. Furthermore, the city has a high population density, which will make it easy to manage in a comprehensive and systematic manner, ensuring compliance and a smooth transition for our entire administration.

Surprisingly, our economists and Foreign Minister Boris Trofimov are taking the opposite view. They propose using the industrial city of Chelyabinsk as the primary, reliable choice, which would serve as a model for other Russian cities to follow. In addition to the industrial factor itself, proponents of this option point to the direct projection of Soviet influence and power into Central Asia. After all, as supporters of this capital expect, it will give us important leverage to influence our main southern neighbor - Kazakhstan, which is weakened by its own internal disputes and regional conflicts.

But it is the NKVD secret police, led by Vasily Blokhin and Stepan Garanin, who want to establish an unconventional capital in the quiet and unremarkable town of Zlatoust. As the saying goes, "demons roam the quiet marshes" - and that's exactly how one might describe this option. Such a place, remote from major Russian cities and well-protected by the Ural Mountains, is definitely to the liking of the executioners who will be carrying out their executions.

So, while one can continue to speculate about the true intentions of those advocating for this mountain city, a decision on a specific and single capital for the new Soviet Union must be made right now. After a brief debates and several sleepless and tense nights, by a decision of the Secretary, supported by the Presidium, it was decided to move the capital from the city of Vorkuta to the city of...

title: Lowest Level of Electricity Supply Ever Agreed Upon
desc:
Busy all day with paperwork, Vasily didn’t notice how quickly the time had flown by. Only after eating and returning to his office did he see that darkness was already falling outside the window, and it was only 3:00 p.m. The issue of restoring water supply to the Pechora Gulag remained unresolved; such humanitarian matters should have been handled by Comrade Trofimov, but he was at negotiations in Arkhangelsk. The fact was that an agreement had been concluded with the Western Russian Revolutionary Front, under which they were to provide electricity in exchange for cheap labor - workers from our country. The Minister of Economy was supposed to oversee this process, but there were increasingly more instances where the agreed-upon energy resources were delivered late, in incomplete quantities, or were completely unsuitable for our extremely cold climate.

But as soon as he opened the document, it had grown so dark that the pages were illegible. The man picked up an old desk lamp, turned it on, but it did not work. He walked over to the light switch in the office and flipped it a few times, and immediately realized there was no power. Losing his temper, he grabbed his desk lamp and hurled it at the front door. It broke in half with a crash, and the loud noise in the hallway caught the attention of other officials, including Deputy Minister of Economy Nikolai Chernenko. He and several others rushed to the office, where their secretary was already raging and shouting at his staff to come out immediately.

"What the hell is this, I ask you - who can explain why there is no electricity in the central government building?! It was working yesterday and even this morning!" the Secretary thundered in a heavy, angry tone.

"C-Comrade Secretary, it is most likely just a power outage; Minister Yudin should have everything sorted out shortly..." the deputy minister replied, barely keeping his composure.

"Are you fucking confused or something? Comrade Nikolai, get in touch with your irresponsible boss right away and explain the situation in the capital, in the government building, which is supposed to have an uninterrupted power supply. And give me a clear answer already: where the hell is the stable power supply Comrade Yevgeniy promised us?!"

A group of officials turned to look at Nikolai; at that moment, he would have preferred to sink into the ground rather than stand there. Swallowing a couple of mouthfuls of saliva that felt like imaginary bullets, he closed his eyes and said:

"We can't get in touch with him because of the power outage... there isn't even enough electricity left to keep the capital running, Comrade Secretary! I am sorry to have to tell you this unpleasant truth, but Comrade Yudin really can't do anything about it. Rather, this needs to be resolved diplomatically!"

After standing there for a few seconds, stamping his feet, Blokhin shouted and took out his anger on the reception desk for other officials standing next to him. One of its four legs snapped off; damaged but not completely broken, it rolled toward the group leader standing opposite him. Vasily wiped his face with his palms, ran his hand down to his nose, and uttered one final sentence before ordering everyone out of the office:

"So everyone listen here - no one has a word about today's situation. Anyone who lets it slip will be fired and imprisoned. Tape up this broken chair with duct tape and tell Yevgeniy Yudin to fix the power outages in the coming months - not just in the capital, but in all the prisons and Gulags across the country! I will no longer tolerate lame excuses that have no basis in reality. Either he takes care of this, or he'll be removed from his position - you're dismissed!"

As everyone quickly dispersed, Blokhin sat down in his chair, staring at the chair he did broken in a fit of rage. In truth, it was not so much anger as complete disappointment in the work of his rogue minister. He would take revenge for all the inconveniences caused to him personally, to his Gulags, and to the diplomatic relations with Arkhangelsk, which would be ruined because of such an unfortunate incident. It was necessary to instruct Trofimov not to pressure or accuse the WRRF of violating agreements caused by our internal abuses by parasites.

title: Persecution of City Dwellers
desc:
In Zlatoust, a city traditionally situated some distance from the country’s central regions, the morning sun had long since ceased to illuminate the gray, multi-story buildings. Nowadays, it was rare to see crowds of people in public places, let alone on ordinary streets. Everything changed with the fall of the Golden Trade Republic and the arrival of the Bolshevik authorities, who were vastly different from those in Tyumen. Vlad had once worked here and run his own independent business selling essential agricultural products. He had contracts with farmers from neighboring villages who supplied him with fresh produce—free of preservatives and, most importantly, fresh and just harvested. In some months, especially during the fall, Dragunov’s government offered to buy up goods for state needs (including for trade), and just when things were going best—new regional wars broke out, the West Siberian Turmoil, which put an end to his business.

It wasn’t long before the region fell under the control of barbarians from the north, who cloaked themselves in the “Bolshevik” mantle of legitimate authority over a destitute people. Unfortunately for small and medium-sized businesses, spontaneous nationalization processes began. The businesses they had built over a lifetime—and the family businesses they had inherited or earned through service to the Soviet Union—were now, ironically, being taken from them in the name of the mythical “achievement of the communist revolution”. At first, Vlad was thrown out onto the street as a former bourgeois—elements hated by the regime—and, using the remaining funds he had hidden away, took up residence with a janitor. A few months after the wave of nationalization, the regime launched a policy of “red collectivization”, arguably its most extreme form. City residents began to be searched en masse on the grounds of "concealing foreign propaganda or other anti-revolutionary luxury items". Vlad felt safe until the very end, since he was living with the janitor, whom the law enforcement agencies would certainly not pay any attention to. And one day, when he was alone in the apartment, there was a knock on the front door after lunch, saying that financial aid had arrived for the janitor to support his situation. Thinking it was the monthly bonus his friend received, the man went and opened the door to the stranger without a second thought. However, they turned out not to be government officials, but five NKVD agents, who immediately burst into the apartment, seized the former entrepreneur, blindfolded him, and then one of them read out the ill-fated official government directive.

"Bourgeois entrepreneur Vlad, whether you are aware of it or not, with the recent adoption and launch of the program approved by the Presidium on the ‘Relocation of City Dwellers to Collective Labor in the Villages’, the emphasis has been placed on those representatives who exploited the peasants, never worked the fields themselves, and merely stole the fruits of others’ labor for their own gain... This has come to an end today with your arrest; you will be sent to perform forced labor at the Chelyabinsk Collective Farm to atone for all your counterrevolutionary actions and the damage inflicted upon the Soviet Union."—one of the NKVD officers spoke in a monotonous, cold, yet confident voice. At first, Vlad tried to struggle and scream, but after a few quick blows to the stomach, his strength to resist was gone.

Deep down, he knew that this day would come once these barbarians from the Russian Arctic North had established their rule. They showed no mercy to their own citizens—their own indigenous people—so what could be said about the entire population of the regions that had fallen under their control? In any case, all these thoughts and possible scenarios no longer mattered; now the real struggle for survival had begun for the townspeople, who were being forcibly sent to the villages for forced labor. The authorities were simply another cog in the machine, using them to mitigate the risk of famine—and, of course, to replenish the state budget with their free labor. After all, just as with war communism, payment here was not made in currency or money in the conventional sense, but in food—to keep these prisoners in the deadly fields of Blokhin’s regime as long as possible, a regime that now operated more on their suffering than on their labor.

“If our future is decided here and now, what will become of the rest of the Russian people when this ruthless secretary establishes his ‘workerist’ government across the entire homeland?”
Vlad, an enslaved worker, murmured quietly, more to himself than to anyone else, as he finished harvesting corn in one of the many rows in the field.

title: Nothing Ever Happens in the Arctic Ocean?
desc:
In the icy Arctic Ocean, months seemed to drag on like days. By controlling the theoretically vital intersection of the Northeast Passage and the Northern Sea Route, the sailors and admirals of the Northern Fleet hoped to dominate this trade route and, at the very least, make money and receive goods in this extreme corner of the world. However, in practice, things turned out to be much bleaker; global trade here was something of a “miracle” that these souls had prayed to God for. In reality, since the end of World War II, humanitarian ships—including American Lend-Lease aid provided to the defeated Soviet Union for several years—did indeed pass through here a few times a year, were it not for the dark cloud hanging over the Novaya Zemlya archipelago.

Sparsely populated and incapable of offering any resistance, these islands were occupied by German admirals and their Kriegsmarine. They similarly occupied the Norwegian archipelago of Svalbard without difficulty, which became a springboard for their further expansion into the Arctic Ocean against our fragmented Union. Like vultures stalking an exhausted, weary, and wounded prey, they pounced at the first opportunity, occupying our “New Land” without resistance and projecting their power ever deeper into the Ocean. The worst thing for us was the mining by their submarines of a section of the Northern Sea Route that was vital to us; American civilian ships began to be blown up and sink as a result. Thus, we were left without a single source of humanitarian aid by sea and found ourselves isolated in Russian anarchy. These difficult times taught us a lesson: if we are not ready for battle, we will lose it. And ever since then, on a regular basis—practically every day—Soviet admirals have been ordering their subordinate sailors to survey the surrounding waters and detect enemy minefields.

Surprisingly, after the end of the Western Russian War, these patrols detected no activity by the enemy Kriegsmarine along our shores; not even a single new instance of mine-laying was observed! This state of affairs was both reassuring and unsettling, as such silence was uncharacteristic of the Germans. A few years later, we understood the reason for the silence—it turned out to be the internal political struggle in the Reich over the legacy of the dying Führer Hitler, which left the troops, particularly the Kriegsmarine, inactive. So, over the past year, sailor Pavel had been conducting a weekly naval patrol along the WSSLR’s coastline; in general, he was lucky, since his friends who served on submarines carried out such patrols several times a week or even every day except weekends. Pavel was a lookout on a destroyer, scanning the tower for the presence of enemies or enemy mines—which, due to the movement of the ice floes, sometimes shifted position quite frequently—and essentially had the primary role in these expeditions. Previously, these patrols were conducted once a month at best, since the country, isolated in Vorkuta, did not have enough fuel for such frequent use of the fleet. However, with the establishment of control over the entire region, the fuel situation became more than favorable for such missions.

However, just as in the previous year, nothing at all has happened this year either, and few people knew why. Everyone predicted that the Kriegsmarine would resume its terrorist activities against its enemies—particularly against the Russian socialists and Bolsheviks—immediately after the end of the German Civil War, but this never happened. Everything remains as calm as it was before they went to war against each other. Despite this, even Golovko himself insists that these coastal patrols have not ceased under any circumstances, despite all our past losses of ships—except for submarines—which were blown up by enemy minefields in this dangerous zone. So, Pavel began his usual shift on a day off for all the other sailors—on the most vulnerable Northern Sea Route. The next 10 hours meant constant strain on his eyes, quick reflexes, and intense focus on everything in front of, to the right, and to the left of the ship.

Nothing happened for the first three hours; they sailed calmly westward from the port in the Salekhard region. There was ice on the port side, so the ship’s crew stayed closer to the safety of land. The following hour, they sailed further north, away from the coast, to survey the occupied archipelago. By the sixth hour of sailing, a total of three mines had been spotted, all of which were easily avoided. Numerous floating icebergs constantly distracted the observer, and this occasionally annoyed him, since these black iron masses, filled with explosives, could be nearby or completely hidden from the observer’s view on the other side of a floating ice structure. And then, just as the sun began to set but still illuminated the path, something did indeed happen during the sailors’ otherwise monotonous expeditions. Pavel initially turned away from the iceberg, not noticing the red hue, but when the sun blinded his right side, the sailor turned his face and binoculars back to the left side and froze—the enemy flag of the Reich was flying on the floating iceberg. Without wasting a moment, Pavel contacted his crew on the ship, and they, in turn, contacted Admiral Sergei Gorshkov within minutes.

“..Comrade Admiral Sergei, this is the crew of the ship ”Golovko" reporting: we are 206 kilometers from the coast to the northwest, 74 kilometers west of the Novaya Zemlya Archipelago, heading 53° northeast. Comrade Observer Pavel reports within visual range: currently, 163 meters from the ship, there is a small iceberg with a Nazi German flag flying on it. The iceberg appears to be 12 meters wide and 7 meters high, drifting south. We await orders on what to do."

“Comrade Petty Officer Viktor, I hear you. Continue monitoring, follow him, and await further instructions. Be prepared to take action against this target in the event of an emergency!” the admiral warned.
