description:
In the icy Arctic Ocean, months seemed to drag on like days. By controlling the theoretically vital intersection of the Northeast Passage and the Northern Sea Route, the sailors and admirals of the Northern Fleet hoped to dominate this trade route and, at the very least, make money and receive goods in this extreme corner of the world. However, in practice, things turned out to be much bleaker; global trade here was something of a “miracle” that these souls had prayed to God for. In reality, since the end of World War II, humanitarian ships—including American Lend-Lease aid provided to the defeated Soviet Union for several years—did indeed pass through here a few times a year, were it not for the dark cloud hanging over the Novaya Zemlya archipelago.

Sparsely populated and incapable of offering any resistance, these islands were occupied by German admirals and their Kriegsmarine. They similarly occupied the Norwegian archipelago of Svalbard without difficulty, which became a springboard for their further expansion into the Arctic Ocean against our fragmented Union. Like vultures stalking an exhausted, weary, and wounded prey, they pounced at the first opportunity, occupying our “New Land” without resistance and projecting their power ever deeper into the Ocean. The worst thing for us was the mining by their submarines of a section of the Northern Sea Route that was vital to us; American civilian ships began to be blown up and sink as a result. Thus, we were left without a single source of humanitarian aid by sea and found ourselves isolated in Russian anarchy. These difficult times taught us a lesson: if we are not ready for battle, we will lose it. And ever since then, on a regular basis—practically every day—Soviet admirals have been ordering their subordinate sailors to survey the surrounding waters and detect enemy minefields.

Surprisingly, after the end of the Western Russian War, these patrols detected no activity by the enemy Kriegsmarine along our shores; not even a single new instance of mine-laying was observed! This state of affairs was both reassuring and unsettling, as such silence was uncharacteristic of the Germans. A few years later, we understood the reason for the silence—it turned out to be the internal political struggle in the Reich over the legacy of the dying Führer Hitler, which left the troops, particularly the Kriegsmarine, inactive. So, over the past year, sailor Pavel had been conducting a weekly naval patrol along the WSSLR’s coastline; in general, he was lucky, since his friends who served on submarines carried out such patrols several times a week or even every day except weekends. Pavel was a lookout on a destroyer, scanning the tower for the presence of enemies or enemy mines—which, due to the movement of the ice floes, sometimes shifted position quite frequently—and essentially had the primary role in these expeditions. Previously, these patrols were conducted once a month at best, since the country, isolated in Vorkuta, did not have enough fuel for such frequent use of the fleet. However, with the establishment of control over the entire region, the fuel situation became more than favorable for such missions.

However, just as in the previous year, nothing at all has happened this year either, and few people knew why. Everyone predicted that the Kriegsmarine would resume its terrorist activities against its enemies—particularly against the Russian socialists and Bolsheviks—immediately after the end of the German Civil War, but this never happened. Everything remains as calm as it was before they went to war against each other. Despite this, even Golovko himself insists that these coastal patrols have not ceased under any circumstances, despite all our past losses of ships—except for submarines—which were blown up by enemy minefields in this dangerous zone. So, Pavel began his usual shift on a day off for all the other sailors—on the most vulnerable Northern Sea Route. The next 10 hours meant constant strain on his eyes, quick reflexes, and intense focus on everything in front of, to the right, and to the left of the ship.

Nothing happened for the first three hours; they sailed calmly westward from the port in the Salekhard region. There was ice on the port side, so the ship’s crew stayed closer to the safety of land. The following hour, they sailed further north, away from the coast, to survey the occupied archipelago. By the sixth hour of sailing, a total of three mines had been spotted, all of which were easily avoided. Numerous floating icebergs constantly distracted the observer, and this occasionally annoyed him, since these black iron masses, filled with explosives, could be nearby or completely hidden from the observer’s view on the other side of a floating ice structure. And then, just as the sun began to set but still illuminated the path, something did indeed happen during the sailors’ otherwise monotonous expeditions. Pavel initially turned away from the iceberg, not noticing the red hue, but when the sun blinded his right side, the sailor turned his face and binoculars back to the left side and froze—the enemy flag of the Reich was flying on the floating iceberg. Without wasting a moment, Pavel contacted his crew on the ship, and they, in turn, contacted Admiral Sergei Gorshkov within minutes.

title: Is it worthwhile to debate the future leadership of the NKVD?
desc:
As time passed more rapidly and the country's territory expanded even more rapidly, an ever-increasing number of conscripts joined the ranks of the various units. The NKVD's elite structure was no exception to this rule, as its new members were generally promoted from the ranks of those recruited from the newly acquired territories. Many of them do not share the same ideological convictions as their commander, Blokhin, and although it is publicly forbidden to even discuss aloud the correctness of actions or express doubts about orders, the soldiers find like-minded individuals.

Despite the adoption of the NKVD Code, over the past year there has been an increase in the formation of secret groups outside the barracks and military bases, where members discuss the authorities’ counterterrorism policies. When mandatory rules regarding guard duty in village garrisons and the execution of disloyal elements who do not submit to the regime are introduced, some NKVD officers carry out parallel orders from the left wing to conscript villagers into forced labor. And this process intensified as Officer Sergei Kruglov's influence within the structure grew. Having risen through the party hierarchy, he became the Secretary's right-hand man, beginning to hand down more “humane” sentences to disobedient citizens.

In fact, this faction of politicians came to be known as the “Kruglovites” or the “left wing of the NKVD,” terms that deliberately downplay or obscure Blokhin's most extreme and deadly directives regarding the suppression of disobedient citizens. The latter is aware of this, but he does not want to disrupt a completely loyal, reliable structure. At times, the dictator does not even consider that his own NKVD structure, which has faithfully served him for more than a decade, is capable of yielding leadership to someone else.

However, there is a corresponding reaction to these challenges: the sergeants themselves, ranking above the ordinary soldier, willingly turn in their comrades who have fallen under the influence of these subversive groups in exchange for generous rewards, thereby currying favor with the regime. Given such a system and hierarchy within the structure, it is difficult to imagine that, during the lifetime of the all-powerful Vasily Blokhin, an internal coup and the ousting of the leader could occur. Moreover, in documentation and during meetings, all prominent and leading members of the NKVD—Stepan Garanin and Sergei Kruglov—express complete loyalty and fidelity to the regime.

After several hours, he decided...

title: Contacts from the Soviet Urals
desc:
After over a decade of isolation from any of their comrades in the other SSRs, Kazakh communists have received a very pleasant surprise: correspondence from the Russians! Diplomats and emissaries from the West Siberian Soviet Labor Republic to the north have journeyed into the region, telling of sympathetic leadership to the north and a revitalized, regime-driven communist workerist system, with a leader keenly aware of the mistakes of the old Soviet Union. They promise that aid, trade, additional worker personal and better relations are just around the corner, as soon as the WSSLR figures out the logistics of sending supplies through the still-turbulent countryside. In the meantime, they plead only for recognition, and an assurance that the Kazakhs and Central Asians will work alongside them for the reconstruction of the Soviet Union when the time comes.
For the Kazakhs and Central Asians, this offer certainly seems tempting. Aid to reconstruct their shattered, underdeveloped economies and arms to fight their petty border wars would certainly be welcomed. A connection to the outside world for the first time in years seems too good to be true. But there are always doubts; what happens if Secretary makes demands that infringe upon their sovereignty? The rumors that trickle out of their capital paint Vasily Blokhin as far more controlling than the rosy picture his diplomats have painted of him might imply. Assuming the Central Asian peoples decide to embark down the path of friendship with the Siberian strongman, they have much to look forward to, and much to be wary of.

title: Purges of "enemies of the regime" in Military Posts
desc:
One signal, one command, and the life of one NKVD officer is interrupted, despite all his previous services to the regime. With the expansion of the secretary's power and control over the whole of Western Russia to the border with the Reichskommissariat, unexpected purges in the troops began. But it is not so much the Red Army that is being repressed as the traditionally loyal structure of the NKVD.

The dictator, reading reports about the resistance in the newly acquired western territories, began to show emotional outbursts in the form of paranoid attacks. No, he does not calm down from stress by eating, smoking or some peaceful hobby, he is "entertained" by the suffering of the population. With the passage of time, it is no longer so exciting for the tyrant, he took up his staff purges.

Either in view of the past, or in view of the international situation with the overthrow of dictatorial regimes, local analysts agree with the failed "putsch" that was carried out by apolitical faction a few months earlier. Since the repression against them is ending, the secretary's bloodthirstiness has not yet been satisfied. He was angry not only at the army, but also at his closest environment, and based on this, paranoia developed acutely. All the assessments of the experts come down to a single conclusion - these are the largest purges in Russia since the Bolshevik revolution, and right now the labels "enemy of the regime" are being applied to the perpetrators of the crimes themselves.

Following the purges of the grassroots, the repression reached its peak - the Minister of Defense himself, Stepan Garanin, was arrested. As a result, the military structure of the Union is currently paralyzed for how long no one knows, but all information inside and outside our country is closed and only information that has been checked and cleared by strict censorship is disseminated. With every new day, there are more and more cases of soldiers voluntarily escaping from the army, suicides have become a common phenomenon, and there are so many sentences - that even weekly norms are not fulfilled, not to mention monthly purges.

title: The Stalemate Needs an Obvious Solution
desc:
"The new wave of purges must end, you can't spend a whole year snubbing and killing your own defenders," said the senior-most elderly man to his assistant, exhaling steam from a cigarette. His assistant, Sasha, glanced at him, interrupting the natural pause in the conversation,

"Yes, enough time has passed to quench Blokhin's thirst for bloodlust, after all, we will come out victorious in this situation!" suddenly lit up the man, who was visibly full of optimism due to the recent chain of promotions of his boss.

After inhaling the remains of a cigarette and exhaling thick smoke, throwing the remains on the ground and trampling it with his boot, he said the following to his closest assistant with a penetrating look:

"Sasha, you have been with me since the beginning of my journey here, back in Vorkuta, I do not want to lie to you, I have changed during this time, deliberately becoming a tool of a comrade secretary. The last wave of purges proved to me that there is no point in being an independent player under Vasily, and I accepted his risky and dangerous order. Tomorrow I was assigned to become the head of the firing squad of Garanin himself, after which - to take the vacant place of the minister security." Sergei said in a cold voice.

The assistant froze for a few seconds, not that he felt sorry for the scumbag Garanin or all the victims of "opponents of the regime", it's just that this sudden change in the tone of his boss and voluntary complete submission to the bloody secretary caught him by surprise. However, he knew the current realities, that refusing any proposal of the secretary could cost his entire career, and probably his life, immediately dispelled all misunderstandings. Smiling and grasping his waist with both hands, he accepted such a dangerous promotion, as he had accepted all previous ones.

title: "Plague-Like" Purges of Disloyal Territories
desc:
The recently formed secret special service "Chuma", as part of a top-secret state program aimed at reorganizing Special Laboratory No. 12 under the leadership of Blokhin's confidant - Alexander Nikolaevich Shelepin, newly appointed in [GetYear] as secretary of the Central Committee of the KPSTS. "Chuma", established within the NKVD, will have as its primary role the suppression of anti-state and anti-regime protests by the population in the liberated west - in effect, it will be an unrestrained "hunt" for dissidents.. Officially, these are operations to ensure the security of the Union, as well as to promote the "restoration" of stability and order in the territories of Western Russia. Unofficially, it involves implementing programs to combat all manifestations of separatism or insurgent movements in disloyal and recently annexed territories of the Soviet Union. However, hidden even from the party will be the statistics - the results of using toxicological, bacterial, and poisonous substances for targets identified by the secret services.

Among them were many viruses familiar in Russia - tuberculosis, anthrax, natural ricin, and others. Local laboratories served as "X"-special chambers, where the effects of the newly created poison were tested on captured dissident prisoners. Another "academician", Muromtsev, head of the bacteriological laboratory in Komi, returned to his research and developed a new type of biological weapon to combat anti-socialist insurgents. According to numerous eyewitness accounts, NKVD troops even added this poison to rural wells and the water supply system in Western Russia. As for gases, the technology for their use was quite simple. An NKVD task force, having surrounded suspicious churches or remote settlements, would identify so-called "vents"-ventilation openings. Through these, via ventilation ducts or openings in the building's structure, they pumped in a highly potent toxic gas that caused severe chemical poisoning and immediate loss of consciousness among the insurgents, allowing them to be neutralized or abducted to "X"-special chambers.

According to Shelepin’s plans, the crowning achievement of the NKVD's secret USLR laboratory was to be a development scheduled for completion around the mid - 1970s. We are talking about a top-secret weapon: According to the project's authors, the weapon was to be used by NKVD agents abroad (primarily in Europe due to economic and technological constraints) to preempt a so-called "RNA" operation ("Rocket-Nuclear Attack") by the Reich. This project is constantly being lobbied for by the current secretary of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of the KPSTS. According to his plan, at the appointed hour "X", NKVD operatives abroad, acting on orders from the residency, were to scatter "through the corridors of power" in the capitals of the Unity Pact member states-for example, in Germania - under the guise of couriers and messengers, in places of mass gathering, and in the their subways, colorless, almost invisible ampoules containing a potent sprayable poison that would instantly kill anyone upon remote activation by an agent.

Currently, this is described in theory as part of long-term plans, but at the same time, secret agents are already putting it into practice against their own rebellious population, traitors within the ranks of the security services, and "enemies of the regime". Hundreds of millions, if not billions, of Soviet rubles are being allocated from the state treasury to fund these programs, as well as to utilize the expertise in the use of chemical and biological arsenals obtained from the Syktyvkar chemical laboratories. We are also utilizing the findings of the now-neutralized Black League, whose professors from biological and chemical research laboratories have been captured by us and are working for our benefit at gunpoint. No one will dare to attack us - neither the Europeans of the Unity Pact nor the Asians of the Japanese Sphere - because if they do, they will deeply regret their hostile intentions against the Secretary's regime...

title: Coordination of Strikes Against Resistance Cells
desc:
This morning, the "Alligator" task force arrived at the mission site on orders from A.N. Shelepin. Consisting of 25 people from Nizhny Tagil, they are part of the extensive network of the secret, reorganized Special Laboratory No. 12 of the NKVD Institute of Special and New Technologies, directed by the regime to brutally suppress resistance to the Union's reestablishment of control over the returned territories. This "Alligator" task force, which replaced the previous "Bears" task force, will spend the next month fighting resistance in Komi and the northern regions...using unconventional methods. Nikolai Bulavin, the unit commander and leader, clearly assigned tasks to the personnel, emphasizing priority actions and objectives.

The first week will be spent keeping quiet and monitoring the locals, and if no suspicious activity is detected, the second week will also be devoted to surveillance. Of course, the agents aren’t stupid; they understand that "enemies of the regime" will hide at every opportunity, which means they'll need to search every street, including the sewer system and nearby forests. During the second and third weeks, there will be house searches; if there is any attempt to resist, individuals will be detained as violators of public order and for obstructing law enforcement activities, and transported to nationalized underground complexes. By the last week of the month, the task force will compile a report on the execution of "counter-insurgency" operations to neutralize local insurgent elements, which must include the elimination of some of the captured dissidents.

desc:
[GetMonth][GetYear], Week 1: The "Alligator" task force arrived at the mission site to relieve the "Bears" task force in the city of Kotlas, where a resistance cell that betrayed our securocratic-workist revolution is located. These {Classified} individuals, who are resisting our civil administration, were spotted during the first week of surveillance at {Classified}, {Classified}, around 7:00-10:00 p.m. At the end of week 1, Nikolai Bulavin decided to infiltrate their structure over the course of the following week, in coordination with headquarters and with the permission of {Classified}.

Week 2: The deputy leader of the traitors and "enemies of the regime" in Kotlas - {Classified} - allowed our agent {Classified} to gain access to their headquarters in a basement facility located at {Classified}, on the outskirts of the city near the river. Over the next few days, we learned of most of their key bases, {Classified} within the city itself and {Classified} outside the city. The information obtained by the task force has been and will continue to be included in the report as the operation proceeds.

Week 3: Permission has been granted to our operational group by {Classified} and Special Laboratory No. 12 to use toxic gas agents and {Classified}, which will cause severe chemical poisoning and immediate loss of consciousness among the traitors at the {Classified} bases, but the operation is expected to be carried out with careful preparation. Additionally, we are requesting permission to conduct similar actions in the outskirts of the city at {Classified} locations. The expected completion time for the operation is approximately at the end of the month - the final week of the special operation. The order {Classified} is clear - to capture the majority of their representatives and command staff alive, by means of {Classified}... in the event of resistance that poses a danger to agents - use {Classified}.

Week 4: Agents of the "Alligator" Task Force have gained access to virtually all safe houses, specifically {Classified}, including underground bunkers and hideouts in and around the city of Kotlas. At half of the locations known to us, {Classified} have been installed to conduct a coordinated simultaneous raid on all known bases of traitors and "enemies of the regime". We are awaiting final instructions and authorization from higher authorities regarding the fight against dissident traitors in the region, as well as {Classified}. Control is being established over the escape routes and access to the secret hideouts of members of the underground {Classified}.

Week 5: Under circumstances that remain unclear to us, {Classified} prior to the raid, our network of agents in {Classified} was exposed, and several agents were captured. On my initiative, in accordance with Protocol {Classified}, without the consent of {Classified}, Special Laboratory No. 12, and without the authorization of {Classified}, all of our prepared toxic biochemical weapons were activated immediately after losing contact with several agents. Unfortunately, it was nighttime, so due to the risk of losing sight of the {Classified} groups, the traitorous saboteurs and "enemies of the regime" were shot after attempting to escape via the routes we had uncovered - {Classified}...

End of monthly report: Due to unforeseen circumstances and the exposure of eight of our agents, as well as the loss of constant contact with them, I, Nikolai Bulavin, have decided to carry out Operation {Classified} ahead of schedule. After a 6-hour early raid, as stipulated in the protocol, we captured a total of 98 immobilized traitors, "enemies of the regime", and killed approximately 204 in the city of Kotlas and beyond. The "Alligator" task force lost 9 rank-and-file members;
the losses are considered significant, and the task force requires regrouping.

title: Discussion of the Necessary Defense Strategy
desc:
With the expansion of the Union's territory into Western Russia as far as the Volga River, it became clear that virtually the entire border region was quite vulnerable. And we’re not talking about the small border with Finland, or the extension of the border with unstable Kazakhstan, which is only just recovering from the devastation, but specifically about the Nazi Pact. Our new neighbors in the form of the Reichskommissariat Moskowien, which are on par with us in terms of population, economy, and, presumably, military strength, are causing considerable concern for our Supreme Command, Presidium, and government. It is dangerous to forget about such neighbors, because even though we had good relations with them at the height of World War II, they treacherously stabbed us in the back and destroyed our unity, strength, and people, pushing us further back from the Volga. Accordingly, Blokhin first entrusted this matter to the ministers so that they could agree on a common position, and then, purely as a formality, the Presidium would adopt whatever strategy of action they proposed.

The issue concerns military affairs, as it pertains to the Soviet Union’s national military strategy in the event of the unthinkable - a new war against the fascist forces of evil in Europe. Therefore, it is the Minister of Defense who is granted carte blanche and the final say on the proposed strategy of confrontation. Starting with the main arguments for a defensive stance, statistics were cited that did not even show parity with our adversaries, since even the detested RK Moscowien, as of [GetYear], surpasses our Union in every respect except for the professionalism of its army. Under such conditions, it is entirely impractical to build an offensive doctrine; further proof of the folly of such actions is the defeat of the West Russian Revolutionary Front in the West Russian War. After analyzing the troops equipped with military hardware, it was acknowledged (though not documented) that less than 30% of the army’s structure was equipped with military hardware (there were not even any armored vehicles).

"Precisely because of all these factors, I won’t even consider - nor do I recommend considering - an offensive strategy; it will be impossible to pull off over the next 3–4 years. So, comrades, we face a major new threat: a border stretching thousands of kilometers with Muscovy - our territories occupied by the nazis. Although I am surprised that during the active conflicts in West Russia, the Germans did not intervene, did not cross the border, and even when we established our undisputed authority in the region..." - he scratched the back of his head, clearly searching for the right words, since the speech was not so much a prepared address as an analysis of the new situation.

“So, Comrade Sergei, do you think they’re afraid of more casualties during the war, or are they simply waiting for a single victor to emerge from the wars in Russian anarchy so they can then strike at the sole surviving ruler of Russia?”, Trofimov broke the silence, wanting to test his new colleague’s professionalism.

“Yes, you're basically right - there's no arguing with that. Those despicable Germans have taken a convenient wait-and-see stance. ‘Why should we die fighting the Russians when we can just wait for them to destroy themselves?’ - that's what those scoundrels are thinking. We’re not fools, and we must join the preemptive game right now by investing in the defense of our temporarily weakened Motherland!”, Kruglov said proudly, rising from his chair. Maltsev gave him a skeptical look, waving his raised hand to bring his colleague back down to earth.

“Comrade, may I remind you that our resources are limited, and building a wall along the entire western border will cost hundreds of millions of rubles. Because of your project, which is mandatory under our defense strategy, we will deplete our last reserves and risk losing the funds needed to finance the upcoming war in Siberia!”

"Comrade Mikhail, with all due respect to your work, this is a matter of national survival. Everyone in this room understands this; you must understand it too. If something doesn’t suit you - back it up with documentary evidence; if you can’t do that - don’t stand in my way; it’s not within your authority”, Kruglov replied bluntly and directly to the economist.

After more than an hour of discussion, the parties were ready to submit the defense strategy to the Secretary and the Presidium; they were not concerned with costs - only with the outcome. But will Sergei Kruglov use his new position to increase funding for the construction of a stronger and more reliable system of fortifications along the western border, or will he limit himself to a symbolic, inexpensive, and incomplete line of fortifications?

title: Status of the Redirection in Magnitogorsk
desc:
The Minister of Economy decided to conduct an inspection of the state of local governance in the Southern Urals and the implementation of orders from the capital. In general, due to time constraints, he will not visit every region, but instead has decided to inspect nearby Magnitogorsk. Other districts will be inspected by his aides, comprising his entire cabinet, due to the short timeframe and the vast territory of the Southern Urals. In this economic mission, his ministry would play an observational role and, of course, provide funding to redirect the district’s economy toward military needs. This, incidentally, no longer surprised him, given the systematic militarization of the state in recent years. During these difficult and busy days, he recalled his appointment as minister back in 1962. Back then, the tasks were irregular, isolated, and of course complex, but he set his own work schedule, essentially to consolidate a new economic model that has been functioning almost flawlessly to this day!

Times have changed, and there are more and more tasks that are difficult to delegate to subordinates, due to Blokhin's paranoia toward civil servants and his subordinates of ranks lower than ministers. Consequently, all the heads of ministries tried to personally carry out the orders of the old paranoid man for the sake of their own safety - and even their lives. Everyone remembers well the numerous examples of people being executed, even those in the highest positions at the peak of their careers, simply because they did things "their own way" or failed to carry out the Secretary's instructions at all. But to complain about the current state of affairs is to mock oneself, so Mikhail simply set about silently, without complaint, carrying out the work and duties assigned to him. Arriving on this cold morning at his destination - Magnitogorsk-Gruzovoy railway station, outside the city. First, he surveyed most of the northern infrastructure for entering the city with his personal driver in a rare, government-issued black "Volga" and jotted down the addresses of the district's non-redirected enterprises in his notebook.

After that, having crossed the bridge over the Ural River, he began his inspection of the city itself. Here, the results were already much better; as a demonstration of "responsibility", the northern and central parts of the city had made progress in redirecting light industry toward military production. However, closer to noon, unprepared textile enterprises began to appear, followed by furniture factories and retail centers. The situation was particularly acute in the western and southern parts, where orders for the reorientation had been received but were not being implemented promptly. Although Comrade Maltsev understood what would happen to the leadership and their subordinates in these industrial sectors, he had no room for error in his report. Many of these subordinates, who thought they could circumvent "party policy" and stay on the sidelines, peacefully continuing to amass small to enormous fortunes, even begged and offered bribes to "embellish" the report and mask the true state of affairs. Mikhail was no fool, but he agreed with everyone, taking their money in exchange for silence and falsifying reports - which he never did. In fact, for every such incident, immediately after getting into the "Volga" - which had a phone built into the body-he would call the NKVD leadership and report on new "enemies of the regime" and the security-bureaucratic revolution.

By around ten o'clock that evening, the tour of the entire city was complete, and Mikhail Maltsev was returning to his reserved train for the trip back to the capital. He had no energy left to enter the records into the database or even send instructions to his ministry via phone, so he went to bed with a stack of documented violations committed by business owners. The train was due to depart within the next few minutes, so before falling asleep, he thought once more about these unfortunate souls who had decided to simply do things their own way in a country where freedom of choice doesn't exist. Surely, within the course of this week, all their businesses would be nationalized by the state, and their current leadership - repressed. It was clear that the managers faced execution by firing squad, while all their subordinates, simply for working under these managers, would be repressed and sent to the correctional labor camps in the vast rural areas of the Union.

There was a jolt, the engine roared to life, and the train pulled away, gradually picking up speed. The minister didn't dwell on today; he had done everything right to prove his efficiency and loyalty to Comrade Secretary Vasily once again - just as he had done yesterday, the day before, and every time before that - simply to ensure he could carry on living the days ahead.

title: Introduction of a Century of Forced Labor
desc:
It was a quiet evening in Kazan, and its residents were simply looking forward to a stable tomorrow. We are talking about the so-called minorities - people of other ethnicities, cultures, religions, or faiths; in general, it doesn’t matter. It was mostly Russians who were deported from the cities to "correctional labor camps"; the authorities had branded them as a "declining people", which is why they were treated somewhat worse than other nationalities. Until then, they had been left alone because they were few in number, at least in the region of Western Siberia; however, to the west of the Ural Mountains, they are an order of magnitude more. Thus, the ruling regime faced a dilemma: the abuse of its relatively free position by other nationalities in a country where communist equality was proclaimed. This state of affairs even reached the General Secretary himself, so it was necessary to somehow rectify the situation.

Strangely enough, what would seem to be a purely domestic matter was assigned to Minister Boris Trofimov, who specialized in foreign affairs. Presumably, due to someone's irresponsible - and even treacherous - performance of their duties, this complex issue somehow leaked out, beyond the borders of the nascent Union. Boris was fully aware of the threat posed by continued neglect of this issue, and alongside the closure of the state border to the entire population, a thorough reform of the chaos must be carried out, along with the subsequent concealment of any internal situation that might leak out. Border patrols will be strengthened to apprehend "enemies of the regime" attempting to cross the border illegally, and the NKVD will be given the green light to conduct an urgent investigation of the entire leadership of the ministries of internal and foreign affairs for the presence of "moles". At the same time, all citizens and national minorities within USLR-controlled territories will be granted equal rights so that no ethnic group begins to shun national programs. It has been decided to initially conduct the experiment in the country's most separatist region - Tatarstan - and, following the successful implementation of the new policy there, to apply this approach to all other regions.

Literally a week later, the matter was settled by the act "On the Mandatory Nature of Corrective Labor for Future Generations", with a validity period of 100 years, though without the possibility of further extension. This act was adopted by the Presidium without changes, although initially it referred only to a quarter of a century - 25 years of forced labor - but Blokhin, at his insistence, increased this figure to a full century. In fact, from the moment this act is ratified as of [GetYear], it will be valid and enforced by the population for the next 100 years. It is entirely logical that once its contents are made public, it will significantly reduce population growth, but families will be informed of its existence after the birth of their child. In the event of refusal to comply with the act, the child will be legally taken from the parents and placed in an orphanage. The idea is simple: future generations of citizens born after this law takes effect will be automatically sent to work on collective farms to enrich the Motherland. For this purpose, it is not necessary to verify whether a person is considered an adult or still a minor; everyone will be treated equally. According to the government's optimistic projections, this decision will draw in three or more generations to work, providing them with employment. As a result, several problems will be solved at once - the very existence of poverty, discrimination, and the lack of equality - and it will eliminate manifestations of separatism in the Soviet Union, since the act applies to the entire future population regardless of race, membership in any national minority, or whether they are children of foreigners.

This act will also contribute to accelerated assimilation, and the Secretary-General's signature will mean that he will abide by it for as long as the dictator lives. The people of Tatarstan have finally come face-to-face with the harsh reality of living under a securocratic-workerist regime and are now forced to comply with the relevant legislation. They are no longer consulted, and authorities are beginning to treat them as if they were part of the indigenous population. More and more ethnic Tatars are being sent to "correctional labor camps" and collective farms, with no right to leave their confines, and their descendants and future generations of Tatars will likely be gradually assimilated. After all, what better unites an ethnically diverse population than shared forced labor or life under unbearable conditions?

As a result, having helped carry out a successful experiment in Tatarstan within a record-short timeframe, Trofimov turned his attention to the USLR international image, where he will not even attempt to build any relations with non-socialist countries. His country has chosen the path of a hermit, isolated from the international arena and relying solely on itself. Following the recent adoption of the "On the Mandatory Nature of Corrective Labor for Future Generations (Correctional Labor Century)" act and official policy, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has adopted a stance of closing itself off from foreign attention. Thus, all foreign media and journalists, without exception - even those from friendly socialist countries - will not be allowed into the territory of the Union. Control over our own officials will be tightened and will continue to be strengthened to prevent, under any circumstances, the dissemination of information regarding our domestic policy. And our decrees on forced labor will continue to apply to our entire population, for the sake of our survival in a world that is unfriendly and even hostile toward us.

As a result, several problems will be solved at once - the very existence of poverty, discrimination, and the lack of equality - and it will eliminate manifestations of separatism in the Soviet Union, since the act applies to the entire future population regardless of race, membership in any national minority, or whether they are children of foreigners.

This act will also contribute to accelerated assimilation, and the Secretary-General's signature will mean that he will abide by it for as long as the dictator lives. The people of Tatarstan have finally come face-to-face with the harsh reality of living under a securocratic-workerist regime and are now forced to comply with the relevant legislation. They are no longer consulted, and authorities are beginning to treat them as if they were part of the indigenous population. More and more ethnic Tatars are being sent to "correctional labor camps" and collective farms, with no right to leave their confines, and their descendants and future generations of Tatars will likely be gradually assimilated. After all, what better unites an ethnically diverse population than shared forced labor or life under unbearable conditions?

As a result, having helped carry out a successful experiment in Tatarstan within a record-short timeframe, Trofimov turned his attention to the USLR international image, where he will not even attempt to build any relations with non-socialist countries. His country has chosen the path of a hermit, isolated from the international arena and relying solely on itself. Following the recent adoption of the "On the Mandatory Nature of Corrective Labor for Future Generations (Correctional Labor Century)" act and official policy, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has adopted a stance of closing itself off from foreign attention. Thus, all foreign media and journalists, without exception - even those from friendly socialist countries - will not be allowed into the territory of the Union. Control over our own officials will be tightened and will continue to be strengthened to prevent, under any circumstances, the dissemination of information regarding our domestic policy. And our decrees on forced labor will continue to apply to our entire population, for the sake of our survival in a world that is unfriendly and even hostile toward us.

title: vorkuta.main.13.t
desc:
The system, which was systematically built on fear, hard labour, the authority of the state, punitive squads and so on, has endured. The entity which experts had predicted would inevitably collapse over time continues to stand firmly on its own two feet, having even quashed any thoughts of uprising or protest amongst its own population. An atmosphere of fear pervades everyone, without exception, regardless of ethnic origin or position held, as even the leader of the Union of Soviet Labor Republics, Vasily Blokhin, fears any protest or even demonstrative movement within his domain. Purges, punishments and repressions continue in a frenzy against all those who disagree with the ruling regime's policy, a regime that has survived and functions thanks to the country's multi-vector existence.

And the structure built up over the last decade functions symbolically, as long as the heart of its unique and bloodthirsty leader continues to beat. A peculiar cycle, designed to ensure total control and keep the entire population occupied, guarantees the continuity of Blokhin's rule and the loyalty of his own government, party, ministers and generals. Other factions are either subjugated to his will or eliminated and repressed for his personal ends, which can now be fully realised without external threats from rival Russian governments. But what will the dictatorial regime do, after the unification of Russia, with no other rival for legitimacy and unity of power as the last heir to the old Soviet Union?

Of course, the "Great Purge" - so named by analogy with Stalin's theories on preserving the authority of the regime - is still underway, but it is already on the wane and drawing to a close. The regime has held firm, loyalty is secured, and now Vasily himself must naturally hold firm. At the moment of Russia's complete unification, he would have analyzed all his forces and resources, and continued to use all of Motherland's boundless resources to his own advantage. However, unexpectedly, the enemies are running out, and we are not talking about "enemies of the regime", of whom there will always be plenty, but specifically about an external threat - on whom to hang the next noose for the sake of the dominance of his own USLR and the purged party?

He will have time for all of this, since none of the surrounding threats pose any immediate danger, and he now has a free hand - for the first time in three decades. Vasily is the undisputed ruler of the Soviet Union; his own people and foreign delegations from other countries must reckon with him. No one tells him what to do or gets in the way of his policies anymore, and as a bonus, he rules the world's largest country by area, though it's still far from prosperity and the peak of its power. What the General Secretary knew for certain was the inevitability of a new war against Nazi and fascist forces in Europe, for which the country must be fully prepared. To this end, the people - the entire population of the Union - will be mobilized to work under increased quotas, under constant surveillance by the NKVD. Some would work day and night if necessary to accelerate the readiness of the Soviet Union - lagging a whole decade behind - to confront its ideological enemies on the international stage.

After all, the securocratic-workerist revolution did not rule out the victory of the proletariat worldwide and the overthrow of the global bourgeoisie. Having begun in our Motherland, we will continue to move step by step toward the overthrow of all imperialist and exploitative capitalist regimes throughout the world, until the enslaved peoples are liberated, having chosen the socialist path we desire. And the unification of Russia under Vasily Blokhin is not only the triumph of his ideological struggle, but the beginning of what the world will eventually come to call...

title: Death of the Bloodiest Executioner of Russia
desc:
At the beginning of [GetYear], on January 7, the Union of Soviet Labor Republics celebrated another birthday of Vasily Blokhin, the infamous tradition of "calling" was held as usual. The Secretary personally visited 2 Gulags, in which he ordered the execution of 137 prisoners due to the worst quota of the specified labor plan. Other prisoners in the second Gulag were not given food during the day, to test their endurance before the arrival of the dictator in the evening, due to which several dozen lost consciousness and were liquidated. The Union does not tolerate weak persons, they are the first to be hit by routine health checks. And the punishment of such violators of discipline is a lesson for other prisoners, which must be learned and worked harder.

In short, the Soviet Union lived its new but familiar life until this day. The unthinkable happened, what all party members, generals, ministers and Blokhin's closest entourage were afraid of - he died in his sleep. Quietly, without even making a single sound, is probably the best death for the most bloodthirsty Russian leader. According to the protocol, the person who was closest to the General Secretary in terms of status and position should have received power, but in our case it is two persons at once. General Secretary of the Central Committee of the KPSTS - Alexander Shelepin and the de facto heir of the secretary in the structure of the NKVD - Sergey Kruglov. The next few days after the death of Vasily Blokhin, these two began to act in advance against each other, putting sticks in the opponent's wheels and turning others against their enemy. However, it was the new head of the NKVD who had greater authority, who used his loyal soldiers to first arrest Shelepin's closest entourage, and after accumulating enough compromising material, to arrest his main rival. So, even in the absence of a mechanism for the transfer of power or a recognized sole heir of the deceased Vasily, Sergey Kruglov became the new General Secretary of the USLR.

With the goal of improving the management of the Soviet Union and reducing the obvious bureaucratic problems in the administration, he will take several key steps in the coming months. First, it is a problem with separatism, which is determined to continue rooting out opposition to the legitimate Soviet rule throughout the vast Motherland. Secondly, it is the reform of the administration itself, starting with reducing the number of party officials in the Presidium by half and renaming it to the "Supreme Presidium of the USLR", renewing ineffective personnel that delay the adoption of various laws. Third, he intends to replace most, if not all, civil administrations west of the Urals with military commissariats controlled by his secret police.

And, his most important goal is to finally reject Blokhin's legacy in the form of the NKVD crowd, which has grown. We are talking about the predominance of special operational troops of the NKVD over the regular Red Army, due to which the former have become less professional and effective in recent years. Therefore, the essence of the reform will consist in changing the name of the structure from "NKVD" to "KGB" (State Security Committee), and several times increasing the requirements for new soldiers who want to join the ranks of the KGB in the future.The current military personnel belonging to the NKVD will be tested for their suitability and professionalism, and based on this, it will be decided whether to leave them for the future. All these reforms will require time and effort, which General Secretary Kruglov is ready to spend. After all, otherwise, in his opinion, the regime will collapse in the long term, and the Union of Soviet Labor Republics itself will collapse under its own weight, unable to stand on its feet.

title: A Putsch, Carried Out by an Apoliticals
desc:
It was a typical cold morning in the capital, and nothing out of the ordinary was expected. Just another workday for factory workers, their guards, and the city's civilian population in general. But the usual loud signal from the loudspeakers mounted on every corner of the identical buildings did not sound; everything was quiet. Historians will mark this day as the "End of Tyranny", characterized by the spontaneous paralysis of the entire regime's system due to the coordinated actions of an apolitical faction led not so much by military officers and generals as by noble sailors. These maritime patriots, weary of lawlessness and the deteriorating social situation on land, having gained sufficient influence in the Union - which appears to be living out its final days - rallied around the renowned Admiral Arseniy Golovko to put an end to the securocratic-workerist experiment once and for all!

Whether the preparations took weeks, months, or even years no longer matters, since overnight all key district administrations were disarmed, and the administrations - not without the barrel of an AKM at their throats - sided with the unexpected coup. Everything went down without bloodshed; the much-praised but increasingly corrupt NKVD units in the barracks were captured by the Admiral's troops. The empty Presidium was also seized to prevent a counter-coup and any retaliatory actions by party faction members.

But the question regarding the ministers and the tyrant Blokhin himself remains open, as there is no confirmation of their capture. Initially, two Red Guard units were dispatched to their locations, one for each target; to our surprise, no reports followed from them afterward. Due to the loss of communication, three additional military units from Yugra and one from Omsk - formed a year ago - have been dispatched. We await the earliest possible confirmation of the ministers' capture and, most importantly, that of the vermin Blokhin, who will undoubtedly face punishment for all the crimes he has committed!

title: Was Golovko's Coup...a Success?
desc:
Finally, urgent messages arrived directly to the admiral from apolitical units tasked with capturing the entire ruling elite of the criminal, securocratic-workerist regime. Out of impatience, hastily tearing open the sealed message from his soldiers, confident that justice would prevail, Arseniy didn't even read the introductory section detailing the units that had completed their missions. He immediately skipped to the main body, which contained the bad news for the country's new de facto leader. This was not a failure of the mission - it was a catastrophe for his movement and the entire apolitical faction that had successfully overthrown a regime which had terrorized its own people with impunity for a long period. However, every new sentence in the letter saddened and angered the admiral more and more, confirming all his deepest fears.

"We must report the complete failure of the operation to capture representatives of the criminal securocratic-workerist regime... a betrayal within our ranks led to the disclosure of all key figures in the government and among the ministers... As for the Secretary, unfortunately, he was the first to be evacuated when we began our operation and took the first settlements in the north and center of the country... also, most likely, other ministers and the majority of the government were evacuated... to an unknown destination; it seems they already had a contingency plan in place for internal unrest... So we won't be able to try that old bastard to the full extent of the updated law due to betrayal within our own ranks. CONCLUSION: The guilty fugitives are two units of the Red Guard, who evacuated beyond the country's borders along with the regime's top leadership.” The admiral read aloud nervously to all his new followers and colleagues who would now lead the country.

Everyone was silent, glancing first at one another and then at the floor, unable to find the words. The situation was shameful, not just for the new government, but for the entire nation, which would not see justice served to the executioners and inhuman criminals who had tormented them for so long. For Arseniy Golovko in particular, it was a blow to his pride and confidence in his actions, so he had to remain silent for several dozen seconds along with the crowd of future politicians. However, surprisingly, his colleague in naval affairs - Sergei Gorshkov - broke the silence, suddenly stepping in front of Arseniy, taking his hand, and turning to the crowd. With a confident expression on his face, and to boost the spirits of everyone gathered at this meeting before they officially took their new government posts, Gorshkov raised the leader's hand and shouted to everyone:

title: Long-awaited Fruits of the Market Economy
desc:
Slowly but surely, the transition from a planned to a market economy seems to have finally started yielding positive results! Several reports submitted to the president's office over the past week only confirm this. Arseniy hadn't expected it to happen so quickly. No, he knew that once control was gained over Magadan, a city crucial for trade sphere, the situation would improve, but it didn't even take a few years! And now, taking his time, he made himself a cup of tea, settled into his chair in his office, and read the first report of the week from his Minister of Economy.

"The result of international treaties": While we were isolated in the Arctic, there was no one with whom to conclude new trade agreements, since ships from other countries - with the exception of some American vessels - were unable to regularly supply us with goods, even as far as the port of Arkhangelsk. The Arctic Ocean is the coldest of all, so sailors tend to avoid it. However, with our recent acquisition of control over the port of Magadan, we have gained a unique opportunity to conclude new trade agreements not only with Asian countries, particularly Japan, but also with Latin American countries. We expect the arrival of new merchant ships within days; this will be noted in subsequent reports. Sincerely, Minister of Economy - Georgy Gins.

"An encouraging first report from the minister", the admiral said to himself with a smile, taking a long sip of tea. Getting ready to read on, he skipped a few related follow-up reports and glanced over the infrastructure reports. Up to that point, he had been concerned about Magadan's suitability for such broad and diverse trade with the world. Several consecutive reports confirmed the port's capacity to handle a large number of merchant ships per day. At the same time, photographic evidence showed the city's survival following the establishment of federal control over it. So, putting aside all further concerns, he moved on to the latest report, submitted over the weekend.

"The road to a "sea-trading" market economy continues": Mr. President, we have already recorded more than 20 port shipments in four days, which is an extremely encouraging result of your efforts to transition to a market economy. Yes, these are only the first steps toward opening up our riches to the world, for which there is frenzied demand and which promises great profit. Shortly after establishing control over Magadan, we have, as of now, signed trade agreements with countries such as: the United States, Canada, Ecuador, Chile, the Japanese Empire, the Republic of China, the Philippines, Indonesia, and India. This openness from the international community, facilitated by the unification of Russia under our Federation's banner, will allow us to fully transition to a market economy and fully join the global trade system in the near future (5-7 years)! Sincerely, Minister of Economy - Georgy Gins.

Everything was proceeding as planned, including the reorientation of the economic system, which would no longer rely on unreliable plans. Much of the credit for this goes to Gins, who seemed to have easily "mastered" the planned targets by combining them with the "sea-trading" elements of a market economy. Arseniy stood up and looked out the window at the sun setting beyond the horizon. His task was complex, and the assignments given to his staff were new; some struggled with even basic tasks, such as implementing capitalist reforms in rural areas. However, the trade and economic sector in particular delighted him more than any other sector in the country. A few years would pass, and Russia would stand firmly on its own two feet, which would mean...

title: Consideration of Ministerial Candidacies
desc:
When considering candidates, the leader should take into account the background of all contenders. The main contenders are the opinion leaders among the democratic reformers of the system, and they are the focus of attention for both the public and politicians. But they are pioneers in a country that has long suppressed the individualism and freedoms of its citizens, so it will be easy for them to gain public support in a short time. So it all comes down to Arseniy's personal signature in favor of one candidate or another, and without the unnecessary bureaucracy that is only just taking shape, it will be easy and quick to appoint a new face to the post of minister.

The Federation's Ministry of Foreign Affairs is the only one among all the others that has not yet begun to perform its functions due to the extremely advanced age of its former head, which is why the country has effectively remained in isolation. title: Future of the Infamous VEOP
desc:
With the fall of the criminal tyrannical regime and the failure of the securocratic-workerist revolution, we were left with the legacy of their misguided policies. These policies were explicitly aimed at impoverishing all segments of the population, consolidating the regime, and preparing for new wars with our neighbors. The list of these programs is long, and each claimed the lives of prisoners or ordinary citizens who were unlucky enough to be in the wrong place at the wrong time. But there is one militarized program that, in fact, continues to operate to this day - the Military Economic Orientation Program. Its premise is simple: to spend about 25% of our annual income on the development of our armed forces, a policy that was relevant specifically during the active phase of the wars against the warlords, our Russian rivals. Thus, its relevance has run its course, since we will not start new wars, either before or after unification, unless our national interests are threatened.

It was entirely conceived and pushed through by the now-infamous former Minister of Defense, Stepan Garanin. Following the declassification of files, there is ample evidence and confirmation of the program's core objective: a war aimed at spreading a securocratic-workerist revolution across the globe. Of course, these utterly insane plans were halted by our coup, but we see certain prospects in retaining - or rather, reorganizing - this program. It has benefited our armed forces, which have acquired modern equipment and weapons and have become larger and more professional. But everyone without exception in the ministries and the government agrees that the level of spending must be reduced by at least five times. New expenditures for the maintenance and operations of the VEOP will amount to 5% of the annual budget, ensuring a fair distribution of funds to other sectors of the economy. Through this plan, we will prevent the depletion of our economy and reduce our debt, while also maintaining our armed forces at an appropriate level.

However, wouldn't this be seen as a threat to our democratic dream? The military, which we wanted to keep separate from the ruling ideology, will receive twice as much funding as provided for in the draft of our future constitution. This also directly contradicts the interests of both civilians and small and medium-sized businesses, which will receive less funding. The president should carefully consider this decision and whether he himself will violate his own slogans and his promise to the people to eradicate and destroy all the evil brought about by the failed securocratic-workerist experiment...

title: Historic Speech in the Duma
desc:
It was a tense day for the State Duma - a reshuffled and reorganized Presidium that had been passing "De-Blokhininization laws" for 30 hours straight, with only brief interruptions. They were adopted with the aim of dismantling all the achievements of criminal securoratic-workerism regime, including all forms of exploitation of the population, of which there were still many. The President made it clear that within a single session, without postponing any other actions, the entire bizarre, inhumane legislative framework from the era of the tyrant Blokhin must be dismantled, including the recognition of him as a war criminal and a "Russian murderer, a executioner in power". In conclusion, a list of all the crimes he had committed was to be compiled and clearly enumerated. As a result, this list exceeded the 10 A4 pages allocated for it, taking up twice as much space - 20 pages - which was intended to shock the entire international community upon publication in the near future. And when the Duma had finished repealing all the tyrant's laws and decrees from the entire period of his reign - which would never again be enforced - the deputies invited the president to deliver his historic speech.

Representatives of media outlets not subject to censorship, international observers, journalists, and experts from committees investigating crimes committed by the former securocratic-workerist regime against the population, among others, gathered. Under the lenses of several cameras, the president of [VOR.GetName], Arseniy Golovko, stepped out onto the stage to loud applause from the audience. Determined, he approached his desk, pushed back his chair - deciding to stand during his speech to appear more resolute and convincing - and opened his notebook. Next to him, he saw a list of all the crimes committed by the previous terrorist regime - those same shocking 20 pages - but he had no intention of reading them aloud. On the contrary, he handed it to the media for their review, as he himself found it repulsive to announce this and waste everyone's time by reading out such a volume of information. So, focusing on his prepared speech, he adjusted his microphone and began to read.

"My fellow russians, the minorities of the Federation, the free media, and the entire free world, I wish to inform you of the De-Blokhinization carried out by my government, the Duma, and my officials. Its purpose is not only to investigate all the crimes of Blokhin's regime and document the course of the bloody securocratic-workerist revolution, but also to achieve practical results in the country's recovery. We have finally put an end to forced correctional labor of citizens and the entire population in the economic and social spheres! The processes of releasing Gulag prisoners and closing torture prisons are still ongoing, but soon every criminal will get what they deserve under our lawful justice!" - a pause as he turned the page was accompanied by loud applause and cheers from the audience. Arseniy didn't want to get distracted so as not to lose momentum, so he continued reading:

"Our national campaign to rid our homeland of the legacy of the war criminal and executioner Blokhin will continue into the new decade and will persist until every criminal who carried out his orders, either directly or indirectly, has been brought to justice! All reforms and changes that will accompany the course of justice include the liberalization of social and political life, the reduction of censorship, and the elimination of ideological control over the population. Citizens will be personally free, and in their daily lives they will not fear law enforcement agencies, which will now work for the well-being of the population, not the ruling regime. All those convicted under the shameful label of "enemy of the regime" will be rehabilitated in the absence of crimes in the traditional, legal sense. We will also eradicate all manifestations of the cult of Blokhin's personality; we will rename the cities named in his honor, we will prosecute all his supporters, and we will destroy all monuments and literature that condone the crimes committed!" - after a pause, another round of loud applause briefly disrupted the president's concentration; he even glanced around the hall and smiled at the cameras. Since he had lost his reading rhythm, he continued by speaking his own thoughts, without even reading the prepared text.

"Thus, all perpetrators will receive sentences commensurate with the severity of their crimes. During my term, at least until official elections are held, my government and the State Duma as a whole will promote the development of democracy, grant rights and responsibilities to our people to establish the rule of law, and improve the international image of the Russian Federation. This is a crucial milestone in the history of the entire Russian people, who have realized their true lack of rights and broken the shackles of a tyrannical regime! With the help of my fellow citizens, I will continue on this difficult path - the path of reform and democratization in all spheres of public life - toward a successful future! Thank you for your attention, dear colleagues!" - Upon concluding his address to the hall, applause lasted for several minutes, and the president happily continued to answer all the journalists' questions. The committees took note of everything and were ready to continue implementing the planned De-Blokhinization for as long as necessary, until the last executioner is punished, whether within the Federation or beyond its borders.

title: vorkuta.golovko.6.t
desc:
With the successful implementation of most of its reforms - including the revision of the old communist constitution to make it more democratic, the establishment of a multi-party system, and the delegation of powers to local administrations in the districts - life is becoming freer and gradually returning to normal. After decades of repression, intimidation, and forced labor to sustain an unstable regime that collapsed under the weight of its own burdens, for the first time since the March Revolution of 1917, the Russian people are able to live for themselves. At the same time, however, it is becoming increasingly difficult to implement all these changes, as the State Duma has begun to break free from direct subordination to the president. The coalition of politicians and deputies united around the leader is already making it clear that this is a temporary arrangement, and that once all crises are resolved, elections will be necessary.

Although the likely presidential candidates are pursuing their own interests - the so-called "privatization", or the state's policy of transferring former state-controlled enterprises into private ownership - this process is quite chaotic and rapid, primarily due to the extraordinary activity and interest of the politicians themselves. The most striking examples are two completely different, opposing forces that are beginning to form their own political blocs in partnership with business. One is the traditional enterprise "VorkutaUgol", which has come under the personal control of Stepan Dyogtev, who proposes to combine the policies of the former regime with new democratic changes. The movement is not popular on a national scale but is more localized, garnering support in the regions of Vorkuta, Ukhta, and, to some extent, Nizhny Tagil. On the opposite side of the political arena stands Boris Yeltsin, a conservative populist once popular in Sverdlovsk, who advocates for broader privatization for the entire population, the enshrinement of fundamental human rights and freedoms, and a ban on extremist forces that would only harm the republic. He himself recently succeeded in privatizing "GazProm" into his own possession, thanks to local connections and exploiting loopholes in the law, which does not yet restrict politicians from owning their own businesses. There are also other political forces just beginning to emerge in the young Federation, which tolerates and allows the emergence of all other opposition forces.

Thus, while laws are only just beginning to take shape and the power structure is only just becoming decentralized, Arseniy Golovko has little time, and he understands what needs his attention. The old sailor has stepped onto a battlefield that is not his own - the land, where the laws by which he continues to live do not apply; here there is a swarm of parasites and beasts that must be restrained or eliminated. Beyond our borders lies a dark world, dimly illuminated by our light of democracy. But fortunately, there are other forces in this world capable of standing up to all the darkness - the Organization of Free Nations; their support for our young Federation will be key, if not decisive, in the new decade. We have overcome the plague of the securocratic-workerist tyrannical regime, suffering countless losses; yet, unfortunately, this is only the beginning of the true trial that the world will eventually call...

title: Financing an Infrastructure Project
desc:
After studying the detailed map of the new areas where his infrastructure projects would continue, Mikhail let out a heavy sigh. As he climbed higher and higher, the weight of responsibility for taking the next steps in his career grew heavier and heavier. He had at his disposal all the wealth and transportation logistics of the the reviving West Siberian Soviet Labour Union, yet deep down he realized that he no longer even controlled his own life. A vicious cycle had already formed: serving and fulfilling all the Secretary’s whims, submitting particularly or completely falsified reports on the implementation of various programs, and backroom deals with the “Workerist-Men” (those who control the majority of key means of production and the enslaved workers).

Of course, reports are very easy to forge, to substitute others, to request more funding, since he is at the top of the financial hierarchy, where everyone blindly follows his documentation and instructions. Maltsev was never an optimist, nor did he aspire to be one; he was a realist. After all, if no one speaks out about corruption and it is never mentioned at the Plenums of the VKP(b), is it worth fighting against something that does not exist de jure? Under conditions of repressive purges against anyone who speaks out about the real state of affairs, as well as punishments such as removal from office or, even worse, being sent straight to the hellish Gulags, no one wants to go against the current—a turbulent and unstable one.

So, which regional area will we choose this time for the construction and implementation of the Maltsev Infrastructure Expansion Plan?
